title.zh: 卷一百十七 列傳第五 諸王二
title.raw: 卷一百十七 列傳第五 諸王二 Volume 117 Biographies 5: Princes 2

sentences.zh: 蜀王椿 湘王柏 代王桂 襄垣王遜燂 靈丘王遜烇 成𨨣 廷鄣 肅王楧 遼王植 慶王㮵 寧王權

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Chun, Prince of Xiang Bai, Prince of Dai Gui, Prince of Xiangyuan Xunxie, Prince of Lingqiu Xunkan, Chengshu, Tingzhang, Prince of Su Yang, Prince of Liao Zhi, Prince of Qing Shu, Prince of Ning Quan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Shu (Chun), Xiang (Bai), Dai (Gui), Xiangyuan (Xunxie), Lingqiu (Xunkan), Chengshu, Tingzhang, Su (Yang), Liao (Zhi), Qing (Shu), and Ning (Quan).

sentences.zh: 蜀獻王椿，太祖第十一子，洪武十一年封。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Shu, Chun, was the eleventh son of the Taizu Emperor and was enfeoffed in the eleventh year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Shu, Chun, was the Taizu Emperor's eleventh son and received his princely title in the eleventh year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 十八年命駐鳳陽。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to reside at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Hongwu he was ordered to take up residence at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 二十三年就藩成都。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he went to his fief at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he went to establish his princely court at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 性孝友慈祥，博綜典籍，容止都雅，帝嘗呼為「蜀秀才」。

translations.literal: By nature he was filial, friendly, and kind; broadly versed in the classics; his bearing refined and elegant—the emperor once called him "the Scholar of Shu."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial, affectionate, and benevolent, widely read in the classics, and graceful in deportment; the emperor once nicknamed him "the Scholar of Shu."

sentences.zh: 在鳳陽時，闢西堂，延李叔荊、蘇伯衡商榷文史。

translations.literal: While at Fengyang, he opened the West Hall and invited Li Shujing and Su Boxing to discuss literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: During his stay at Fengyang he established the West Hall and invited Li Shujing and Su Boxing to debate literature and history with him.

sentences.zh: 既至蜀，聘方孝孺為世子傅，表其居曰「正學」，以風蜀人。

translations.literal: Once in Shu, he engaged Fang Xiaoru as tutor to the heir, named his residence "Correct Learning," to set an example for the people of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After arriving in Shu he appointed Fang Xiaoru tutor to his heir, named his residence "Correct Learning," and thereby set a moral example for the people of Shu.

sentences.zh: 詣講郡學，知諸博士貧，分祿餼之，月一石，後為定制。

translations.literal: He went to lecture at the prefectural school; learning that the academicians were poor, he divided his stipend grain to feed them—one shi per month—which later became a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: He went to lecture at the prefectural school and, finding the academicians impoverished, shared out part of his stipend grain for their support—one shi per month—a practice that later became permanent custom.

sentences.zh: 造安車賜長史陳南賓。

translations.literal: He had a comfortable carriage made and presented it to Chief Administrator Chen Nanbin.
translations.idiomatic: He had a comfortable carriage built and presented it to his chief administrator, Chen Nanbin.

sentences.zh: 聞義烏王紳賢，聘至，待以客禮。

translations.literal: Hearing that Wang Shen of Yiwu was worthy, he summoned him and treated him with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wang Shen of Yiwu was a man of talent, he invited him and received him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 紳父禕死雲南，往求遺骼，資給之。

translations.literal: Shen's father Yi had died in Yunnan; he went to seek the remains and supplied funds.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's father Yi had died in Yunnan; Chun went to recover his remains and provided financial support for the undertaking.

sentences.zh: 時諸王皆備邊練士卒，椿獨以禮教守西陲。

translations.literal: At that time all princes drilled troops on the frontier; Chun alone guarded the western borderlands through ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the other princes all trained troops on the frontier, but Chun alone secured the western marches through moral instruction and ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 番人入寇，燒黑崖關。

translations.literal: When the barbarians raided, they burned Heiya Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier tribes raided, they burned Heiya Pass.

sentences.zh: 椿請於朝，遣都指揮瞿能隨涼國公藍玉出大渡河邀擊之。

translations.literal: Chun petitioned the court, which dispatched Commander-in-chief Qu Neng to accompany the Duke of Liangguo Lan Yu beyond the Dadu River to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Chun petitioned the court, which sent the commander-in-chief Qu Neng with the Duke of Liangguo, Lan Yu, across the Dadu River to intercept the raiders.

sentences.zh: 自是番人讋伏。

translations.literal: From then on the barbarians were cowed and submissive.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the frontier peoples were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 前代兩川之亂，皆因內地不逞者鉤致為患。

translations.literal: Disorder in the two Shu regions in previous dynasties had all arisen because malcontents from the interior incited trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The turmoil that had afflicted the two Shu regions in earlier ages had always been stirred up by malcontents from the interior who provoked the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 有司私市蠻中物，或需索啟爭端。

translations.literal: Officials privately traded for goods from the barbarian lands, or demanded items and provoked quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials privately traded for goods from the tribal lands, or made extortionate demands that sparked conflict.

sentences.zh: 椿請繒錦香扇之屬，從王邸定為常貢，此外悉免宣索。

translations.literal: Chun requested that silk, brocade, fragrant fans, and the like be fixed as regular tribute from the princely residence, and that all other requisitions be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Chun petitioned that silk, brocade, fragrant fans, and similar items be set as the princely household's fixed tribute, and that all other requisitions from the tribes be abolished.

sentences.zh: 蜀人由此安業，日益殷富。

translations.literal: The people of Shu thereby lived in peace, growing ever more prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were thereby able to pursue their livelihoods in peace and grew steadily more prosperous.

sentences.zh: 川中二百年不被兵革，椿力也。

translations.literal: For two hundred years the region was untroubled by war—that was Chun's doing.
translations.idiomatic: For two hundred years the Sichuan basin knew no warfare—an achievement owed to Chun.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，來朝。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, Chun came to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengzu Emperor acceded, Chun came to court.

sentences.zh: 賜予倍諸藩。

translations.literal: He was rewarded twice what other fiefs received.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted gifts twice those given to the other princely houses.

sentences.zh: 谷王橞，椿母弟也，圖不軌。

translations.literal: Prince of Gu Yi was Chun's younger brother by the same mother and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Gu, Yi, was Chun's younger brother by the same mother and was plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 椿子悅燇，獲咎於椿，走橞所，橞稱為故建文君以詭衆。

translations.literal: Chun's son Yueran, having incurred his father's wrath, fled to Yi's residence; Yi proclaimed him the former Jianwen Emperor to deceive the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's son Yueran, having fallen out with his father, fled to Yi; Yi passed him off as the former Jianwen Emperor in order to deceive the people.

sentences.zh: 永樂十四年，椿暴其罪。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yongle, Chun exposed his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yongle, Chun publicly exposed Yi's crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「王此舉，周公安王室之心也。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "Your action, Royal Brother, is the heart of the Duke of Zhou in securing the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Your action, Royal Brother, shows the same devotion to the royal house that the Duke of Zhou showed."

sentences.zh: 」入朝，賚金銀繒綵鉅萬。

translations.literal: When he came to court, he was granted gold, silver, silks, and brocades in vast quantities.
translations.idiomatic: On his visit to court he was rewarded with gold, silver, silks, and brocades in vast quantities.

sentences.zh: 二十一年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 世子悅熑先卒，孫靖王友堉嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Yueran died first; the grandson Prince Jing Youkan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Yueran had died earlier; the grandson, Prince Jing Youkan, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 初，華陽王悅爠謀奪嫡，椿覺之，會有他過，杖之百，將械於朝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Huayang Yueruo had plotted to seize the succession; Chun detected it; when he committed another offense, Chun had him beaten a hundred strokes and was about to send him in fetters to court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Huayang, Yueruo, had plotted to displace the legitimate heir; Chun discovered it, and when Yueruo committed another offense Chun had him beaten a hundred times and was about to send him to court in chains.

sentences.zh: 友堉為力請，得釋。

translations.literal: Youkan pleaded earnestly on his behalf and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Youkan pleaded earnestly on his behalf and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 椿之薨，友堉方在京師，悅爠竊王帑，友堉歸不問。

translations.literal: When Chun died, Youkan was in the capital; Yueruo stole from the princely treasury, but when Youkan returned he did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Chun died, Youkan was in the capital; Yueruo stole from the princely treasury, but when Youkan returned home he did not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 悅爠更誣奏友堉怨誹。

translations.literal: Yueruo further lodged a false accusation that Youkan had spoken resentfully and slanderously.
translations.idiomatic: Yueruo then lodged a false accusation that Youkan had spoken resentfully and slanderously of the throne.

sentences.zh: 成祖召入訊之，會崩。

translations.literal: Chengzu summoned him for questioning, but the emperor died in the meantime.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu summoned Youkan for questioning, but the emperor died before the matter was concluded.

sentences.zh: 仁宗察其誣，命歸藩。

translations.literal: Renzong saw through the false accusation and ordered him to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong Emperor saw through the false charge and ordered Youkan to return to his fief.

sentences.zh: 召悅爠，悅爠猶執奏，仁宗抵其章於地，遷之武岡，復遷澧州。

translations.literal: Yueruo was summoned; he still persisted in his memorial; Renzong dashed his petition to the ground, transferred him to Wugang, and later to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yueruo was summoned, but he still persisted in his accusations; Renzong dashed his memorial to the ground, transferred him to Wugang, and later moved him again to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，總兵官陳懷奏都司私遺蜀邸砲，用以警夜，非制。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande, Commander-in-chief Chen Huai memorialized that the regional command had privately given cannon to the Shu princely residence for night watches, contrary to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xuande, the commander-in-chief Chen Huai reported that the regional command had privately supplied cannon to the Shu princely residence for night watches—a breach of regulations.

sentences.zh: 詔逮都司首領官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the arrest of the leading officers of the regional command.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the arrest of the regional command's senior officers.

sentences.zh: 明年獻還二護衞。

translations.literal: The next year he offered to return two guard units.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he offered to return two guard units to the state.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 是年薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 妃李、侍姬黃皆自經以殉。

translations.literal: Consort Li and the concubine Huang both hanged themselves to follow him in death.
translations.idiomatic: His consort Li and his concubine Huang both hanged themselves to follow him in death.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟僖王友土黨由羅江王嗣，九年薨。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Prince Xi Youtudang succeeded from the title of Prince of Luojiang and died in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his younger brother, Prince Xi Youtudang, succeeded from the rank of Prince of Luojiang and died in the ninth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 獻王第五子和王悅𤉎由保寧王嗣，天順五年薨。

translations.literal: The fifth son of Prince Xian, Prince He Yuexie, succeeded from the title of Prince of Baoning and died in the fifth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian's fifth son, Prince He Yuexie, succeeded from the rank of Prince of Baoning and died in the fifth year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 繼妃徐氏，年二十六，不食死，諡靜節。

translations.literal: His successor consort, the Lady Xu, aged twenty-six, died by refusing food and was posthumously titled Jingjie.
translations.idiomatic: His successor consort, Lady Xu, aged twenty-six, starved herself to death and was posthumously honored as Jingjie (Serene Integrity).

sentences.zh: 子定王友垓嗣，七年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding Yougai succeeded and died in the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Ding Yougai, succeeded and died in the seventh year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子懷王申鈘嗣，成化七年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Huai Shenmin succeeded and died in the seventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Huai Shenmin, succeeded and died in the seventh year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 弟惠王申鑿嗣，弘治六年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince Hui Shenzao succeeded and died in the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Prince Hui Shenzao, succeeded and died in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 子昭王賓瀚嗣，正德三年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Zhao Binhan succeeded and died in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Zhao Binhan, succeeded and died in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 子成王讓栩嗣。

translations.literal: His son Prince Cheng Rangxu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Cheng Rangxu, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 自椿以下四世七王，幾百五十年，皆檢飭守禮法，好學能文。

translations.literal: From Chun through four generations and seven princes, nearly a hundred and fifty years, all were self-restrained, observed ritual and law, loved learning, and were skilled in letters.
translations.idiomatic: From Chun down through four generations and seven princes—nearly a hundred and fifty years in all—they were uniformly self-disciplined, observant of ritual and law, devoted to learning, and accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 孝宗恒稱蜀多賢王，舉獻王家範為諸宗法。

translations.literal: Xiaozong often said that Shu had many worthy princes and held up the household of Prince Xian as the model for all clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaozong Emperor often remarked that Shu produced many worthy princes and held up Prince Xian's household as the model for all imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 讓栩尤賢明，喜儒雅，不邇聲伎，創義學，修水利，振災卹荒。

translations.literal: Rangxu was especially worthy and enlightened; he delighted in refined learning, kept away from music and entertainers, founded charity schools, repaired waterworks, and relieved disaster and famine.
translations.idiomatic: Rangxu was especially worthy and enlightened: he delighted in refined scholarship, shunned music and entertainers, founded charity schools, repaired irrigation works, and provided relief in times of disaster and famine.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十五年，巡撫都御史吳山、巡按御史金粲以聞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing, Grand Coordinator Wu Shan and Investigating Censor Jin Can reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing, the grand coordinator Wu Shan and the investigating censor Jin Can reported his conduct to the throne.

sentences.zh: 賜敕嘉獎，署坊表曰「忠孝賢良」。

translations.literal: An edict of commendation was granted, and a plaque was inscribed "Loyal, Filial, Worthy, and Good."
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict of commendation and had a plaque inscribed with the words "Loyal, Filial, Worthy, and Good."

sentences.zh: 二十年建太廟，獻黃金六十斤，白金六百斤。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when the Grand Temple was built, he presented sixty jin of gold and six hundred jin of silver.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Temple was built in the twentieth year, he presented sixty jin of gold and six hundred jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 酬以玉帶幣帛。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with a jade belt and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him with a jade belt and silks.

sentences.zh: 二十六年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 子康王承爚嗣，三十七年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Kang Chengyao succeeded and died in the thirty-seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Kang Chengyao, succeeded and died in the thirty-seventh year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子端王宣圻嗣，萬曆四十年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Duan Xuanqi succeeded and died in the fortieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Duan Xuanqi, succeeded and died in the fortieth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 子恭王奉銓嗣，四十三年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Gong Fengquan succeeded and died in the forty-third year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Gong Fengquan, succeeded and died in the forty-third year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子至澍嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhishu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhishu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，京師陷，蜀尚無恙。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen, when the capital fell, Shu was still unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, when the capital fell, Shu remained untouched.

sentences.zh: 未幾，張獻忠陷成都，合宗被害，至澍率妃妾投於井。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Xianzhong took Chengdu; the entire clan was killed; Zhishu led his consorts and concubines into a well.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhang Xianzhong captured Chengdu; the entire princely clan was slaughtered, and Zhishu led his consorts and concubines into a well to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 湘獻王柏，太祖第十二子。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Xiang, Bai, was the twelfth son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Xiang, Bai, was the Taizu Emperor's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the eleventh year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received his princely title in the eleventh year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 十八年就藩荊州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he went to his fief at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Hongwu he established his princely court at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 性嗜學，讀書每至夜分。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning and read books often until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was devoted to learning and often read far into the night.

sentences.zh: 開景元閣，招納俊乂，日事校讐，志在經國。

translations.literal: He opened the Jingyuan Pavilion, recruited talented men, daily engaged in textual collation, and aspired to govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Jingyuan Pavilion, gathered talented scholars, devoted himself daily to textual collation, and aspired to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 喜談兵，膂力過人，善弓矢刀槊，馳馬若飛。

translations.literal: He delighted in discussing warfare; his physical strength surpassed others'; he was skilled with bow, arrow, blade, and spear, and galloped as if flying.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in military affairs; his strength was exceptional; he was skilled with bow, arrow, blade, and spear, and rode at a gallop as though flying.

sentences.zh: 三十年五月，同楚王楨討古州蠻，每出入，縹囊載書以隨，遇山水勝境，輒徘徊終日。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirtieth year, together with Prince of Chu Zhen he campaigned against the Guzhou tribes; whenever he went out, he carried books in a silk bag; encountering fine scenery of mountains and waters, he would linger all day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirtieth year he joined the Prince of Chu, Zhen, in campaigning against the Guzhou tribes; on every expedition he carried books in a silk pouch, and whenever he came upon fine mountain or river scenery he would linger there all day.

sentences.zh: 尤善道家言，自號紫虛子。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in Daoist teachings and styled himself Master Purple Void.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in Daoist teachings and styled himself the Master of Purple Void.

sentences.zh: 建文初，有告柏反者，帝遣使即訊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen, someone accused Bai of rebellion; the emperor sent envoys to question him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign someone accused Bai of rebellion, and the emperor sent envoys to question him immediately.

sentences.zh: 柏懼，無以自明，闔宮焚死。

translations.literal: Bai was afraid and unable to clear himself; the entire household burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: Bai, in fear and unable to clear himself, set fire to the palace and perished with his entire household.

sentences.zh: 諡曰戾。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Li (Perverse).
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Li (Perverse).

sentences.zh: 王無子，封除。

translations.literal: The prince had no son; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The prince left no son, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，改諡獻，置祠官守其園。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, his title was changed to Xian (Offering), and temple officers were appointed to guard his estate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign his posthumous title was changed to Xian (Offering), and temple officers were appointed to maintain his estate.

sentences.zh: 代簡王桂，太祖第十三子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Dai, Gui, was the thirteenth son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Dai, Gui, was the Taizu Emperor's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年封豫王，二十五年改封代。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu; in the twenty-fifth year his title was changed to Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu; in the twenty-fifth year his title was changed to Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 是年就藩大同。

translations.literal: That same year he went to his fief at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he established his princely court at Datong.

sentences.zh: 糧餉艱遠，令立衞屯田以省轉運。

translations.literal: Because grain and supplies were hard to transport over long distances, he was ordered to establish garrison farms to reduce transport.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain and supplies were costly to transport over long distances, he was ordered to establish garrison farms to reduce the need for long-distance transport.

sentences.zh: 明年詔帥護衞兵出塞，受晉王節制。

translations.literal: The next year an edict ordered him to lead his guard troops beyond the frontier, under the command of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict ordered him to lead his guard troops beyond the frontier, placing him under the command of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 桂性暴，建文時，以罪廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Gui was violent by nature; during Jianwen, for crimes he was degraded to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was violent by nature; during the Jianwen reign he was stripped of his title and reduced to commoner status for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，復爵。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, his title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengzu Emperor acceded, Gui's princely title was restored.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年正月還舊封。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yongle he returned to his former fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yongle he returned to his former fief at Datong.

sentences.zh: 十一月賜璽書曰：「聞弟縱戮取財，國人甚苦，告者數矣，且王獨不記建文時耶？

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an imperial letter was granted, saying: "I hear, Younger Brother, that you indulge in killing and seize wealth; the people of your domain suffer greatly, and complaints have come repeatedly—does Your Highness alone not remember the Jianwen years?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor sent him a sealed letter: "I hear, Younger Brother, that you indulge in violence and seize wealth; the people of your domain suffer greatly, and complaints have come repeatedly—has Your Highness forgotten what happened in the Jianwen years?"

sentences.zh: 」尋命有司，自今王府不得擅役軍民、斂財物，聽者治之。

translations.literal: Soon officials were ordered that from then on princely residences must not arbitrarily impress soldiers and civilians or levy goods; violators would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward officials were ordered that, from then on, princely households must not arbitrarily impress soldiers and civilians or levy goods; violators would be punished.

sentences.zh: 已復有告其不軌者，賜敕列其三十二罪，召入朝，不至。

translations.literal: Later there were again reports of his disloyalty; an edict listed thirty-two crimes and summoned him to court, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Later fresh reports of disloyalty arrived; an edict listed thirty-two offenses and summoned him to court, but he did not come.

sentences.zh: 再召，至中途，遣還，革其三護衞及官屬。

translations.literal: Summoned again, he reached midway and was sent back; his three guard units and staff were stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned a second time he set out but was turned back halfway; his three guard units and their officers were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 王妃中山王徐達女，仁孝文皇后妹也，驕妒，嘗漆桂二侍女為癩。

translations.literal: The princess consort was a daughter of Prince Zhongshan Xu Da and younger sister of the Renxiao Empress; proud and jealous, she once painted two of Gui's maidservants with lacquer to make them leprous.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was a daughter of Prince Zhongshan Xu Da and younger sister of the Renxiao Empress; proud and jealous, she once smeared lacquer on two of Gui's maidservants to disfigure them like lepers.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝以中山王故，不罪。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor, for Prince Zhongshan's sake, did not punish her.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, the emperor, out of regard for Prince Zhongshan Xu Da, did not punish her.

sentences.zh: 桂移怒世子遜煓，出其母子居外舍。

translations.literal: Gui shifted his anger to the heir Xunduan and expelled mother and son to live in an outer lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Gui turned his anger on the heir Xunduan and expelled mother and son to live in an outer lodge.

sentences.zh: 桂已老，尚時時與諸子遜炓、遜焴窄衣禿帽，遊行市中，袖錘斧傷人。

translations.literal: Gui was already old, yet still from time to time with his sons Xunjiao and Xunyun, in tight clothes and bald caps, roamed the market streets, carrying hammers and axes in their sleeves to injure people.
translations.idiomatic: Though already advanced in years, Gui still roamed the market streets from time to time with his sons Xunjiao and Xunyun, dressed in tight clothes and bald caps, carrying hammers and axes in their sleeves with which to assault passersby.

sentences.zh: 王府教授楊普上言：「遜炓狎軍人武亮，與博戲，致箠殺軍人。

translations.literal: The princely residence instructor Yang Pu memorialized: "Xunjiao consorts with the soldier Wu Liang, gambles with him, and caused the beating death of a soldier."
translations.idiomatic: The princely household instructor Yang Pu memorialized: "Xunjiao keeps company with the soldier Wu Liang, gambles with him, and in the course of a game caused a soldier to be beaten to death."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷杖治亮，降敕責戒，稍斂戢。

translations.literal: The court had Liang beaten with the rod, issued an edict of rebuke and warning, and the misconduct was somewhat curbed.
translations.idiomatic: The court had Liang beaten with the rod, issued an edict of rebuke and warning, and the misconduct was somewhat curbed.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月復護衞及官屬。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year the guard units and staff were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year his guard units and their officers were restored.

sentences.zh: 正統十一年，桂薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhengtong, Gui died.
translations.idiomatic: Gui died in the eleventh year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 世子遜煓先卒，孫隱王仕㙻嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Xunduan died first; the grandson Prince Yin Shixie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Xunduan had died earlier; the grandson, Prince Yin Shixie, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，嘗上言總兵官郭登守城功，朝廷為勞登。

translations.literal: During Jingtai he once memorialized on the merits of Commander-in-chief Guo Deng in defending the city; the court rewarded Deng in response.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he once memorialized praising the commander-in-chief Guo Deng for his merits in defending the city, and the court rewarded Deng in response.

sentences.zh: 天順七年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 子惠王成鍊嗣，弘治二年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Hui Chenglian succeeded and died in the second year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Hui Chenglian, succeeded and died in the second year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 子聰沫先封武邑王，以肆酒革爵。

translations.literal: His son Congmo had first been enfeoffed as Prince of Wuyi but was stripped of his title for drunken misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congmo had first been enfeoffed as Prince of Wuyi but lost his title for habitual drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 已，居惠王喪，益淫酗，廢為庶人，遷太原。

translations.literal: Later, while in mourning for Prince Hui, he became even more debauched and drunken; he was degraded to commoner status and moved to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while mourning Prince Hui, he became even more dissolute and was reduced to commoner status and relocated to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 久之，惠王妃為疏理，復封武邑王，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while, Prince Hui's consort petitioned on his behalf; he was restored as Prince of Wuyi and later died.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Prince Hui's consort pleaded his case; he was restored as Prince of Wuyi and later died.

sentences.zh: 子懿王俊杖襲封代王。

translations.literal: His son Prince Yi Junzhang succeeded to the title of Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Yi Junzhang, succeeded as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，大同軍叛，圍王宮，俊杖走免。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing the Datong troops rebelled and besieged the princely palace; Junzhang fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing the Datong garrison mutinied and besieged the princely palace; Junzhang fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 事平，賜書慰問。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, an imperial letter of consolation was sent.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, the emperor sent a letter of consolation.

sentences.zh: 六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 子昭王充燿嗣。

translations.literal: His son Prince Zhao Chongyao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Zhao Chongyao, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 十二年，大同軍又叛，充燿走宣府，再賜慰問。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Datong troops rebelled again; Chongyao fled to Xuanfu and was again granted imperial consolation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Datong garrison mutinied again; Chongyao fled to Xuanfu and again received an imperial letter of consolation.

sentences.zh: 事平，返國，奏：「亂賊既除，軍民交困，乞遣大臣振撫。

translations.literal: When order was restored and he returned to his fief, he memorialized: "Now that the rebels have been eliminated, soldiers and civilians alike are in distress; I beg that high officials be sent to provide relief and pacification."
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he returned to his fief and memorialized: "Now that the rebels have been eliminated, soldiers and civilians alike are in distress; I beg that senior officials be sent to provide relief and pacification."

sentences.zh: 」詔允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，和川奉國將軍充灼坐罪奪祿，怨充燿不為解，乃與襄垣中尉充耿謀引敵入大同殺王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Hechuan Defender of the State Chongzhuo was stripped of his stipend for a crime; resenting that Chongyao would not intercede for him, he conspired with the Xiangyuan Assistant Commander Chonggeng to lure the enemy into Datong to kill the prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the Hechuan Defender of the State Chongzhuo was stripped of his stipend for a crime; resenting Chongyao's refusal to intercede, he conspired with the Xiangyuan Assistant Commander Chonggeng to lure enemies into Datong to kill the prince.

sentences.zh: 會應州人羅廷璽等以白蓮教惑衆，見充灼為妖言，因畫策，約奉小王子入塞，藉其兵攻鴈門，取平陽，立充灼為主，事定，即計殺小王子。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Luo Tingxi of Yingzhou and others used the White Lotus teaching to delude the people; seeing Chongzhuo as a figure for their sorcery, they devised a plan to bring in the Little Prince beyond the frontier, use his troops to attack Yanmen and take Pingyang, set up Chongzhuo as ruler, and once the affair was settled kill the Little Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Luo Tingxi of Yingzhou and others used the White Lotus teaching to delude the masses; taking Chongzhuo for their prophet, they plotted to bring the Little Prince through the border, use his troops to attack Yanmen and seize Pingyang, install Chongzhuo as ruler, and then kill the Little Prince once their ends were served.

sentences.zh: 充灼然之。

translations.literal: Chongzhuo agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhuo agreed to the plan.

sentences.zh: 先遣人陰持火箭，焚大同草場五六所，而令通蒙古語者衞奉闌出邊，為總兵周尚文邏卒所獲，並得其所獻小王子表，鞫實以聞。

translations.literal: They first sent men secretly with fire arrows to burn five or six grass depots at Datong, and dispatched Wei Fenglan, who spoke Mongolian, beyond the border; he was seized by patrol troops of Commander-in-chief Zhou Shangwen, together with the letter of submission to the Little Prince; after interrogation the facts were reported.
translations.idiomatic: They first sent men secretly with fire arrows to burn five or six fodder depots at Datong, and sent Wei Fenglan, who spoke Mongolian, beyond the border; Zhou Shangwen's patrol troops seized him together with the letter of submission to the Little Prince, and after interrogation the facts were reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 逮充灼等至京，賜死，焚其屍，王府長史等官皆逮治。

translations.literal: Chongzhuo and the others were brought to the capital, granted death, and their bodies burned; the princely chief administrator and other officers were also arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhuo and his accomplices were brought to the capital, granted death, and their bodies burned; the princely chief administrator and other officers were also arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 總督侍郎翁萬達疏言：「大同狹瘠，祿餉不支，代宗日繁衍，衆聚而貧。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda memorialized: "Datong is narrow and poor; stipends cannot be met, and the Dai clan grows daily more numerous, crowded together in poverty."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda memorialized: "Datong is narrow and poor; stipends cannot be met, and the Dai clan grows ever more numerous, crowded together in poverty."

sentences.zh: 且地近邊，易生反側。

translations.literal: Moreover the region lies close to the frontier and is prone to unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the region lies on the frontier and is prone to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 請量移和川、昌化諸郡王於山、陝隙地。

translations.literal: He requested that the princes of Hechuan, Changhua, and other commanderies be relocated in measured fashion to vacant lands in Shanxi and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the princes of Hechuan, Changhua, and other commanderies be relocated in measured fashion to vacant lands in Shanxi and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 」詔改遷於山西。

translations.literal: An edict ordered their transfer within Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their transfer within Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 先是，景泰間，昌化王仕墰乞移封，景帝不許，至是乃遷。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Jingtai, Prince of Changhua Shidi had petitioned to move his fief but the Jingdi Emperor had not permitted it; only now was the move carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Jingtai, Prince of Changhua Shidi had petitioned to move his fief but the Jingdi Emperor had refused; only now was the move carried out.

sentences.zh: 代宗自簡至懿。

translations.literal: From Prince Jian down to Prince Yi in the Dai line.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dai line, from Prince Jian down to Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 封郡王者凡二十有三，而外徙者十王。

translations.literal: Twenty-three in all were enfeoffed as commandery princes, of whom ten were moved elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three in all were enfeoffed as commandery princes, of whom ten were moved elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 襄垣王遜燂，簡王第五子，分封蒲州。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangyuan Xunxie was the fifth son of Prince Jian and was enfeoffed at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangyuan Xunxie was the fifth son of Prince Jian and was enfeoffed at Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 諸王就藩後，非請命不得歲時定省。

translations.literal: After princes had gone to their fiefs they could not pay seasonal visits to their parents without imperial permission.
translations.idiomatic: After princes had gone to their fiefs they could not pay seasonal visits to their parents without imperial permission.

sentences.zh: 遜燂念大同不置，作思親篇，詞甚悲切。

translations.literal: Xunxie could not put Datong out of his mind and composed "Thinking of Kin," a work of poignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xunxie could not put Datong out of his mind and composed "Thinking of Kin," a work of poignant grief.

sentences.zh: 其後，宗人聰瀺、聰泈、俊㰙、俊榷、俊𤱧、俊杓、俊噤、充焞，皆嫻於文章。

translations.literal: Later the clansmen Congmei, Congyin, Junqian, Junque, Juntianduo, Junshao, Junjin, and Chongtun were all skilled in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Later the clansmen Congmei, Congyin, Junqian, Junque, Juntianduo, Junshao, Junjin, and Chongtun were all accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 俊噤，字若訥，尤博學，有盛名，不慕榮利。

translations.literal: Junjin, courtesy name Ruone, was especially learned and enjoyed great fame, caring nothing for rank or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Junjin, courtesy name Ruone, was especially learned and enjoyed great fame, caring nothing for rank or profit.

sentences.zh: 姊陵川縣君，適裴禹卿，地震城崩，禹卿死。

translations.literal: His elder sister, the Lady of Lingchuan, married Pei Yuqing; when an earthquake collapsed the city walls Yuqing died.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister, the Lady of Lingchuan, married Pei Yuqing; when an earthquake collapsed the city walls Yuqing was killed.

sentences.zh: 縣君以首觸棺，嘔血卒。

translations.literal: The lady struck her head against the coffin, vomited blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The lady struck her head against the coffin, vomited blood, and died.

sentences.zh: 年二十有一。

translations.literal: She was twenty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 詔諡貞節。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously titled her Zhenjie.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored her as Zhenjie.

sentences.zh: 靈邱王遜烇，簡王第六子。

translations.literal: Prince of Lingqiu Xunkan was the sixth son of Prince Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lingqiu Xunkan was the sixth son of Prince Jian.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the Xuande reign.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 好學工詩，尤善醫，嘗施藥治瘟疫，全活無算。

translations.literal: He loved learning and excelled at poetry, and was especially skilled in medicine; he once distributed medicines to treat plague and saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and excelled at poetry, and was especially skilled in medicine; he once distributed medicines to treat plague and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 子仕𡒳、孫成鈠、曾孫聰滆，三王皆以孝旌。

translations.literal: His son Shibang, grandson Chengbi, and great-grandson Congge—three princes in succession—were all honored for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shibang, grandson Chengbi, and great-grandson Congge—three princes in succession—were all honored for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 聰滆子俊格，能文善書。

translations.literal: Congge's son Junguo was accomplished in letters and skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Congge's son Junguo was accomplished in letters and skilled in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，獻皇儲明堂二頌、興獻帝后挽歌，賜金帛。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he presented two eulogies on the imperial heir and the Bright Hall, and dirges for the Xingxian Emperor and empress; he was rewarded with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign he presented two eulogies on the imperial heir and the Bright Hall, and dirges for the Xingxian Emperor and empress; he was rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 聰滆嘗乞封其孫廷址為曾長孫，禮官奏無故事。

translations.literal: Congge once petitioned to enfeoff his grandson Tingzhi as great-great-grandson heir; the ritual officials reported that there was no precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Congge once petitioned to enfeoff his grandson Tingzhi as great-great-grandson heir; the ritual officials reported that there was no precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝以王壽考，特許之。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering the prince's great age, specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering the prince's great age, specially granted it.

sentences.zh: 已而復封廷址子鼐鐮為玄長孫。

translations.literal: Later he also enfeoffed Tingzhi's son Nailian as great-great-great-grandson heir.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also enfeoffed Tingzhi's son Nailian as great-great-great-grandson heir.

sentences.zh: 聰滆薨，年八十三。

translations.literal: Congge died at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Congge died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 鼐鐮襲高祖爵。

translations.literal: Nailian inherited his great-great-grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: Nailian inherited his great-great-grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 聰滆之從父成䥩亦有孝行，聰滆聞於朝，賜金幣獎諭。

translations.literal: Congge's cousin Chengjinwei also showed filial conduct; Congge reported it to the court and gold and silks were granted in commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Congge's cousin Chengjinwei also showed filial conduct; Congge reported it to the court and gold and silks were granted in commendation.

sentences.zh: 詔禮官自今宗室中孝行卓異如成䥩者，撫、按疏聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ritual officials that from then on, whenever clansmen showed outstanding filial conduct like Chengjinwei, the grand coordinators and investigating censors should report it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ritual officials that from then on, whenever clansmen showed outstanding filial conduct like Chengjinwei, the grand coordinators and investigating censors should report it.

sentences.zh: 又成𨨣者，隰川王諸孫。

translations.literal: There was also Chengshu, a descendant of the Prince of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Chengshu, a descendant of the Prince of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 父仕𡍫，坐罪幽鳳陽，病死。

translations.literal: His father Shixi was imprisoned at Fengyang for a crime and died there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shixi was imprisoned at Fengyang for a crime and died there.

sentences.zh: 成𨨣微服走鳳陽視喪，上疏自劾越禁，乞負父骨歸葬澤州，即不得，願為庶人，止墓側，歲時省視。

translations.literal: Chengshu went in disguise to Fengyang to attend the funeral, memorialized himself for violating the ban, and begged to carry his father's bones back to Zezhou for burial; if that were denied, he asked to become a commoner and remain by the tomb for seasonal visits.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshu went in disguise to Fengyang to attend the funeral, memorialized himself for violating the ban, and begged to carry his father's bones back to Zezhou for burial; if that were denied, he asked to become a commoner and remain by the tomb for seasonal visits.

sentences.zh: 詔許歸葬。

translations.literal: An edict permitted the return and burial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted the return and burial.

sentences.zh: 弟成鐎亦好學，有志槩。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chengjiao also loved learning and had lofty resolve.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chengjiao also loved learning and had lofty resolve.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年上言：「雲中叛卒之變幸獲銷弭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing he memorialized: "The mutiny of the Yunzhong rebels has fortunately been quelled."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing he memorialized: "The mutiny of the Yunzhong rebels has fortunately been quelled."

sentences.zh: 究其釁端，實貪酷官吏激成之。

translations.literal: Investigating its origin, it was in truth provoked by greedy and cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating its origin, it was in truth provoked by greedy and cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 臣慮天下之禍隱於民心，異日不獨雲中而已。

translations.literal: I fear that the empire's calamity lies hidden in the people's hearts, and one day it will not be Yunzhong alone."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that the empire's calamity lies hidden in the people's hearts, and one day it will not be Yunzhong alone."

sentences.zh: 」指陳切直，帝下廷臣飭行。

translations.literal: His pointed and forthright words led the emperor to order the court ministers to enforce reform.
translations.idiomatic: His pointed and forthright words led the emperor to order the court ministers to enforce reform.

sentences.zh: 時以其兄弟為二難焉。

translations.literal: At the time the two brothers were spoken of as twin marvels.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the two brothers were spoken of as twin marvels.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十年，西夏弗寧，山陰王俊柵奏詩八章，寓規諷之旨。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli, when the western Xia was unsettled, Junzha of Shanyin presented eight poems with admonitory intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Wanli, when the western Xia was unsettled, Junzha of Shanyin presented eight poems with admonitory intent.

sentences.zh: 代處塞上，諸宗洊經禍亂，其言皆憂深思遠，有中朝士大夫所不及者。

translations.literal: Dwelling on the frontier, the Dai clansmen had repeatedly suffered turmoil; their words were all deeply concerned and far-seeing, beyond what many court scholars could match.
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling on the frontier, the Dai clansmen had repeatedly suffered turmoil; their words were all deeply concerned and far-seeing, beyond what many court scholars could match.

sentences.zh: 子靖王豪墭嗣，十四年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Jing Haosheng succeeded and died in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Jing Haosheng, succeeded and died in the fourteenth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子惠王恩𨯀。

translations.literal: His son Prince Hui Enhe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Hui Enhe succeeded.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，松滋王府諸宗人恩鑡等闌入荊州府支歲祿，恩𨯀禁之，皆怨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi the clansmen Enzuan and others of the Songzi princely house forced their way into the Jingzhou residence to draw annual stipends; Enhe forbade it and they all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi the clansmen Enzuan and others of the Songzi princely house forced their way into the Jingzhou residence to draw annual stipends; Enhe forbade it and they all resented him.

sentences.zh: 已，儀賓袁鏞復誘恩鑡等招羣小，奪軍民商賈利。

translations.literal: Later the ceremonial son-in-law Yuan Yong again induced Enzuan and others to recruit ruffians and seize profits from soldiers, civilians, and merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Later the ceremonial son-in-law Yuan Yong again induced Enzuan and others to recruit ruffians and seize profits from soldiers, civilians, and merchants.

sentences.zh: 恩𨯀發其事，恩鑡等愈怨，謀殺王。

translations.literal: Enhe exposed the affair; Enzuan and the others grew more resentful and plotted to kill the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Enhe exposed the affair; Enzuan and the others grew more resentful and plotted to kill the prince.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣官按實，幽恩鑡等鳳陽，謫戍其黨有差。

translations.literal: The court sent officials to investigate; Enzuan and others were imprisoned at Fengyang and their followers banished in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent officials to investigate; Enzuan and others were imprisoned at Fengyang and their followers banished in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 恩𨯀陰使送者刑梏之，斃八十餘人。

translations.literal: Enhe secretly had the escorts torture them with cangue and shackles, and more than eighty died.
translations.idiomatic: Enhe secretly had the escorts torture them with cangue and shackles, and more than eighty died.

sentences.zh: 不數日，世子暴卒。

translations.literal: Within a few days the heir apparent died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the heir apparent died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 八年，恩𨯀疽發背薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Enhe died of a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Enhe died of a carbuncle on his back.

sentences.zh: 子恭王寵涭嗣，與弟光澤王寵𤃆友愛，飲食服御必俱。

translations.literal: His son Prince Gong Chongshun succeeded; he and his younger brother Prince of Guangze Chongxi were affectionate and always shared food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Gong Chongshun, succeeded; he and his younger brother Prince of Guangze Chongxi were affectionate and always shared food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 寵𤃆有令德，寵涭有事必咨之後行。

translations.literal: Chongxi had fine character; Chongshun would consult him before acting on any matter.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi had fine character; Chongshun would consult him before acting on any matter.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 子莊王致格嗣，病不視事。

translations.literal: His son Prince Zhuang Zhige succeeded but was ill and did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Zhuang Zhige, succeeded but was ill and did not attend to affairs.

sentences.zh: 妃毛氏明書史，沉毅有斷，中外肅然，賢聲聞天下。

translations.literal: Consort Mao was versed in history, resolute and decisive; within and without all was orderly, and her virtue was famed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Mao was versed in history, resolute and decisive; within and without all was orderly, and her virtue was famed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 慶靖王㮵，太祖第十六子。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Qing, Shu, was the sixteenth son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing of Qing, Shu, was the Taizu Emperor's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received his title in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年就藩寧夏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he went to his fief at Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he established his court at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 以餉未敷，令駐慶陽北古韋州城，就延安、綏、寧租賦。

translations.literal: Because provisions were insufficient, he was ordered to stay at the old Wei prefecture city north of Qingyang and draw grain rents from Yan'an, Sui, and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Because provisions were insufficient, he was ordered to stay at the old Wei prefecture city north of Qingyang and draw grain rents from Yan'an, Sui, and Ning.

sentences.zh: 二十八年詔王理慶陽、寧夏、延安、綏德諸衞軍務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year an edict ordered the prince to administer the military affairs of the guards of Qingyang, Ningxia, Yan'an, and Suide.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year an edict ordered the prince to administer the military affairs of the guards of Qingyang, Ningxia, Yan'an, and Suide.

sentences.zh: 三十年始建邸。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the princely residence was first built.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the princely residence was first built.

sentences.zh: 王好學有文，忠孝出天性。

translations.literal: The prince loved learning and had literary talent; loyalty and filial piety came from his nature.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loved learning and had literary talent; loyalty and filial piety came from his nature.

sentences.zh: 成祖善之，令歲一至韋州度夏。

translations.literal: Chengzu favored him and ordered him to go once a year to Wei prefecture to pass the summer.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu favored him and ordered him to go once a year to Wei prefecture to pass the summer.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，言寧夏卑濕，水泉惡，乞仍居韋。

translations.literal: Early in Xuande he said Ningxia was low, damp, and its springs foul, and begged to remain at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuande he said Ningxia was low, damp, and its springs foul, and begged to remain at Wei.

sentences.zh: 不許，令歲一往來，如成祖時。

translations.literal: This was not permitted; he was ordered to travel back and forth once a year as in Chengzu's time.
translations.idiomatic: This was not permitted; he was ordered to travel back and forth once a year as in Chengzu's time.

sentences.zh: 正統初，寧夏總兵官史昭奏王沮邊務，占靈州草場畜牧，遣使由綏德草地往還，煽惑土民。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengtong the Ningxia commander Shi Zhao memorialized that the prince obstructed frontier affairs, occupied Lingzhou pastures for grazing, sent envoys across Suide grasslands, and incited the tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong the Ningxia commander Shi Zhao memorialized that the prince obstructed frontier affairs, occupied Lingzhou pastures for grazing, sent envoys across Suide grasslands, and incited the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 章未下，或告王閱兵，造戎器，購天文書。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was issued, others reported that the prince reviewed troops, made weapons, and bought books on astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial was issued, others reported that the prince reviewed troops, made weapons, and bought books on astronomy.

sentences.zh: 㮵疑皆昭為之。

translations.literal: Shu suspected it was all Zhao's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Shu suspected it was all Zhao's doing.

sentences.zh: 三年上書，請徙國避昭。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized asking to move his fief to escape Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he memorialized asking to move his fief to escape Zhao.

sentences.zh: 英宗不可，貽書慰諭。

translations.literal: Yingzong refused and sent a letter of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong refused and sent a letter of consolation.

sentences.zh: 其年薨，子康王秩煃嗣。

translations.literal: He died that year; his son Prince Kang Zhihuang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year; his son, Prince Kang Zhihuang, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年以寧夏屢被兵，乞徙內地，不許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, because Ningxia had repeatedly suffered warfare, he petitioned to move inland but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai, because Ningxia had repeatedly suffered warfare, he petitioned to move inland but was refused.

sentences.zh: 成化五年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 子懹王邃𡓱嗣，十五年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Yin Suiji succeeded and died in the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Yin Suiji, succeeded and died in the fifteenth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 弟莊王邃塀嗣，弘治四年薨。

translations.literal: His younger brother Prince Zhuang Suiji succeeded and died in the fourth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Prince Zhuang Suiji, succeeded and died in the fourth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 子恭王寘錖嗣，十一年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Gong Zhizhen succeeded and died in the eleventh year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Gong Zhizhen, succeeded and died in the eleventh year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子定王台浤嗣。

translations.literal: His son Prince Ding Taihong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Ding Taihong, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 正德五年，安化王寘鐇反，台浤稽首行君臣禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde, when Prince of Anhua Zhifan rebelled, Taihong bowed and performed the rites of subject to lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengde, when Prince of Anhua Zhifan rebelled, Taihong bowed and performed the rites of subject to lord.

sentences.zh: 詔削護衞，革祿三之一，戍其承奉、長史。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his guard units and reduced his stipend by one third; his attendants and chief administrator were banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped his guard units and reduced his stipend by one third; his attendants and chief administrator were banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，台浤賄鎮守太監李昕、總兵官种勛，求為奏請復祿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing Taihong bribed the frontier grand eunuch Li Xin and the commander Zhong Xun to memorialize for restoration of his stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing Taihong bribed the frontier grand eunuch Li Xin and the commander Zhong Xun to memorialize for restoration of his stipend.

sentences.zh: 昕、勛不納，台浤銜之。

translations.literal: Xin and Xun would not accept; Taihong bore them a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Xun would not accept; Taihong bore them a grudge.

sentences.zh: 會寧夏衞指揮楊欽等得罪於巡撫都御史張璿，謀藉王殺璿及勛。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Ningxia guard commander Yang Qin and others, having offended Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuan, plotted to use the prince to kill Xuan and Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Ningxia guard commander Yang Qin and others, having offended Grand Coordinator Zhang Xuan, plotted to use the prince to kill Xuan and Xun.

sentences.zh: 事覺，下都司、按察司按治，欽等誣台浤不軌，璿以聞。

translations.literal: When the plot was exposed, the regional command and surveillance commission investigated; Qin and others falsely accused Taihong of disloyalty, and Xuan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, the regional command and surveillance commission investigated; Qin and others falsely accused Taihong of disloyalty, and Xuan reported it.

sentences.zh: 帝使太監扶安、副都御史王時中等復按，上言：「台浤他罪有之，無謀不軌事。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the eunuch Fu An and Vice Censor-in-chief Wang Shizhong and others to reinvestigate; they reported: "Taihong has other faults, but no plot of disloyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Fu An and Vice Censor-in-chief Wang Shizhong and others to reinvestigate; they reported: "Taihong has other faults, but no plot of disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 」詔廷臣定議，坐前屈事寘鐇，蒙恩不悛，煽構羣小，謀害守臣，廢為庶人，留邸，歲與米三百石，以其叔父鞏昌王寘銂攝府事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the court to decide; for his earlier submission to Zhifan, ingratitude after mercy, and inciting ruffians to harm frontier officials, he was degraded to commoner status, kept at the residence with three hundred shi of grain a year, and his uncle Prince of Gongchang Zhizhen was ordered to administer the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the court to decide; for his earlier submission to Zhifan, ingratitude after mercy, and inciting ruffians to harm frontier officials, he was reduced to commoner status, kept at the residence with three hundred shi of grain a year, and his uncle Prince of Gongchang Zhizhen was ordered to administer the princely household.

sentences.zh: 寘銂裁慶邸宮妃薪米，取邸中金帛萬計。

translations.literal: Zhizhen rationed fuel and grain for the consorts and palace women of the Qing residence and took gold and silks from the treasury in sums of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhen rationed fuel and grain for the Qing consorts and palace women and took gold and silks from the treasury in sums of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 台浤子鼒櫍幼失愛於父，逃寘銂所。

translations.literal: Taihong's son Zaizhan, as a child unloved by his father, fled to Zhizhen's household.
translations.idiomatic: Taihong's son Zaizhan, as a child unloved by his father, fled to Zhizhen's household.

sentences.zh: 寘銂造台浤謀逆謠語，使寺人誘鼒櫍吟誦，圖陷台浤自立。

translations.literal: Zhizhen fabricated seditious verses against Taihong and had eunuchs induce Zaizhan to recite them, plotting to frame Taihong and seize the title himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhen fabricated seditious verses against Taihong and had eunuchs induce Zaizhan to recite them, plotting to frame Taihong and seize the title himself.

sentences.zh: 懷王妃王氏奏寘銂裁減衣食，至不能自存。

translations.literal: Consort Wang of Prince Huai memorialized that Zhizhen had cut food and clothing until they could not survive.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang of Prince Huai memorialized that Zhizhen had cut food and clothing until they could not survive.

sentences.zh: 豐林王台瀚亦欲陷寘銂，遂發其瀆亂人倫諸罪。

translations.literal: Prince of Fenglin Taihan also wished to frame Zhizhen and exposed his crimes of violating human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fenglin Taihan also wished to frame Zhizhen and exposed his crimes of violating human relations.

sentences.zh: 驗實，廢為庶人，幽高牆。

translations.literal: The facts were verified; he was degraded to commoner status and imprisoned in the high wall.
translations.idiomatic: The facts were verified; he was reduced to commoner status and imprisoned in the high wall.

sentences.zh: 廷議謂台浤父子乖離，徙台浤西安，而封鼒櫍世子，視府事，十一年十月也。

translations.literal: The court decided that father and son were estranged; Taihong was moved to Xi'an while Zaizhan was enfeoffed as heir to administer the household—in the tenth month of the eleventh year.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that father and son were estranged; Taihong was moved to Xi'an while Zaizhan was enfeoffed as heir to administer the household—in the tenth month of the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 十五年以兩宮徽號恩復台浤冠帶，薨。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, by grace for the empresses' honorific titles, Taihong's cap and belt were restored; he died soon after.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, by grace for the empresses' honorific titles, Taihong's cap and belt were restored; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 鼒櫍先卒，弟惠王鼒枋嗣。

translations.literal: Zaizhan had died earlier; his younger brother Prince Hui Zaifang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zaizhan had died earlier; his younger brother, Prince Hui Zaifang, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 好學樂善，以禮飭諸宗。

translations.literal: He loved learning and delighted in good deeds, restraining the clan by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and delighted in good deeds, restraining the clan by ritual.

sentences.zh: 世宗賜之敕，建坊表之。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor granted him an edict of commendation and erected a commemorative arch.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor granted him an edict of commendation and erected a commemorative arch.

sentences.zh: 寧夏築邊牆，鼒枋出銀米佐工。

translations.literal: When Ningxia built the frontier wall, Zaifang contributed silver and grain to assist the work.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningxia built the frontier wall, Zaifang contributed silver and grain to assist the work.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 子端王倪𤏳嗣，十六年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Duan Nixuan succeeded and died in the sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Duan Nixuan, succeeded and died in the sixteenth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子憲王伸域嗣，十九年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Xian Shenyu succeeded and died in the nineteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Xian Shenyu, succeeded and died in the nineteenth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 明年，寧夏賊哱拜反，王妃方氏匿其子帥鋅地窖中，自經死。

translations.literal: The next year the Ningxia bandit Puba rebelled; Consort Fang hid her son Shuai Xin in a cellar and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Ningxia bandit Puba rebelled; Consort Fang hid her son Shuai Xin in a cellar and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 時壽陽嗣王倪爋，哱拜脅降之，不屈，為所囚。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Shouyang Ni Xuan was in succession; Puba forced him to submit but he would not yield and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince of Shouyang Ni Xuan held the succession; Puba forced him to submit but he would not yield and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 鎮原王伸塇理府事，謀襲賊弗克，府中人皆被殺。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhenyuan Shenjun administered the household and plotted to strike the rebels but failed; everyone in the residence was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhenyuan Shenjun administered the household and plotted to strike the rebels but failed; everyone in the residence was killed.

sentences.zh: 賊平，御史劉芳譽言：「諸宗死節者俱應卹錄，方妃宜建祠旌表。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, Censor Liu Fangyu memorialized: "All clansmen who died for principle should be recorded for relief; Consort Fang should have a shrine and commendatory tablet."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were suppressed, Censor Liu Fangyu memorialized: "All clansmen who died for principle should be recorded for relief; Consort Fang should have a shrine and commendatory tablet."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之，給銀一萬五千兩，分振諸宗人。

translations.literal: An edict approved; fifteen thousand taels of silver were given to relieve the clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved; fifteen thousand taels of silver were given to relieve the clansmen.

sentences.zh: 帥鋅嗣，薨。

translations.literal: Shuai Xin succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shuai Xin inherited the title and soon passed away.

sentences.zh: 子倬㴶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhuo Cong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuo Cong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年，流賊破寧夏，被執。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits captured Ningxia; he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Chongzhen reign, rebel forces overran Ningxia and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 安塞王秩炅，靖王季子也，十二而孤，母位氏誨之。

translations.literal: Prince Anse Zhi Jiong was the youngest son of the Prince of Jing; orphaned at twelve, his mother Lady Wei instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Anse Zhi Jiong was the Prince of Jing's youngest son. Orphaned at twelve, he was raised under the tutelage of his mother, Lady Wei.

sentences.zh: 性通敏，過目不忘，善古文。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick and keen; what he read once he did not forget, and he excelled at ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and retentive, he never forgot what he read once and wrote classical prose with ease.

sentences.zh: 遇縉紳學士，質難辨惑，移日不倦。

translations.literal: When he met gentry scholars he would press hard questions and debate doubts, continuing all day without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met gentry scholars he would press them with hard questions and debate knotty points, talking from dawn to dusk without tiring.

sentences.zh: 所著有隨筆二十卷。

translations.literal: His writings included Random Notes in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Among his writings was Random Notes in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 庶人寘鐇，祖秩炵，靖王第四子也。

translations.literal: The commoner Zhifan—grandson of Zhi Tong, fourth son of the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifan, reduced to commoner status, was the grandson of Zhi Tong and the fourth son of the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 封安化王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Anhua.
translations.idiomatic: He received the title Prince of Anhua.

sentences.zh: 父邃墁，鎮國將軍，以寘鐇襲王爵。

translations.literal: His father Sui Man was a State Defender General; Zhifan inherited the princely title through him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui Man held the rank of State Defender General, and Zhifan succeeded to the princely title through him.

sentences.zh: 性狂誕，相者言其當大貴，巫王九兒教鸚鵡妄言禍福，寘鐇遂覬望非分。

translations.literal: By nature he was wild and reckless; a physiognomist said he was destined for great eminence, and the shaman Wang Jiuer taught a parrot to speak falsely of fortune and misfortune—whereupon Zhifan began to covet what was not his due.
translations.idiomatic: Wild and reckless by nature, he was told by a physiognomist that he was destined for greatness; a shaman named Wang Jiuer taught a parrot to utter false prophecies of fortune and disaster, and Zhifan began to aspire to what was not rightfully his.

sentences.zh: 寧夏指揮周昂，千戶何錦、丁廣，諸衞學生孫景文、孟彬、史連輩，皆往來寘鐇所。

translations.literal: Ningxia Commander Zhou Ang, Battalion Commanders He Jin and Ding Guang, and Guard students Sun Jingwen, Meng Bin, Shi Lian, and others all frequented Zhifan's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia Commander Zhou Ang, Battalion Commanders He Jin and Ding Guang, and guard students including Sun Jingwen, Meng Bin, and Shi Lian all frequented Zhifan's residence.

sentences.zh: 正德五年，帝遣大理少卿周東度寧夏屯田。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde the emperor sent Vice Minister of Justice Zhou Dong to survey Ningxia garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengde the emperor dispatched Vice Minister of Justice Zhou Dong to inspect Ningxia garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 東希劉瑾意，以五十畝為一頃，又畝斂銀為瑾賄，敲扑慘酷，戍將衞卒皆憤怨。

translations.literal: Dong, hoping to please Liu Jin, reckoned fifty mu as one qing and moreover levied silver per mu as a bribe for Jin; his beatings were cruelly harsh, and garrison commanders and guard soldiers all burned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to curry favor with Liu Jin, Dong counted fifty mu as one qing and levied silver per mu as tribute for Jin; his beatings were savage, and frontier commanders and garrison troops seethed with hatred.

sentences.zh: 而巡撫都御史安惟學數杖辱將士妻，將士銜刺骨。

translations.literal: Moreover Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief An Weixue repeatedly had officers' wives beaten and humiliated, and the officers nursed a grudge to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator An Weixue also repeatedly had officers' wives beaten and humiliated, and the troops bore him a grudge that cut to the bone.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇知衆怒，令景文飲諸武臣酒，以言激之，諸武臣多願從寘鐇者。

translations.literal: Zhifan, knowing the crowd's anger, had Jingwen treat the military officers to wine and goaded them with words; many of the officers were willing to follow Zhifan.
translations.idiomatic: Aware of the general fury, Zhifan had Jingwen entertain the military officers with wine and incite them with words; many were ready to follow him.

sentences.zh: 又令人結平虜城戍將及素所厚張欽等。

translations.literal: He also sent men to win over the garrison commander at Pinglu Fort and Zhang Qin and others who had long been close to him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent agents to recruit the garrison commander at Pinglu Fort and such longtime allies as Zhang Qin.

sentences.zh: 會有邊警，參將仇鉞、副總兵楊英帥兵出防禦。

translations.literal: Just then there was a frontier alarm, and Regional Commander Qiu Yue and Vice Commander-in-Chief Yang Ying led troops out to defend.
translations.idiomatic: When a frontier alarm arose, Regional Commander Qiu Yue and Vice Commander-in-Chief Yang Ying marched out to meet it.

sentences.zh: 總兵官姜漢簡銳卒六十人為牙兵，令周昂領之，遂與何錦定約。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Jiang Han picked sixty picked soldiers as his personal guard, put Zhou Ang in command of them, and then made a pact with He Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Jiang Han selected sixty elite soldiers as his personal guard, placed Zhou Ang at their head, and struck a pact with He Jin.

sentences.zh: 四月五日，寘鐇設宴，邀撫、鎮官飲於第，惟學、東不至。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fourth month Zhifan held a banquet and invited the grand coordinator and garrison officials to drink at his residence; Weixue and Dong did not come.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fourth month Zhifan gave a banquet and invited the grand coordinator and garrison officials to his residence; Weixue and Dong stayed away.

sentences.zh: 錦、昂帥牙兵直入，殺姜漢及太監李增、鄧廣於坐，分遣卒殺惟學、東及都指揮楊忠於公署。

translations.literal: Jin and Ang led the personal guard straight in, killing Jiang Han and the eunuchs Li Zeng and Deng Guang at table, and separately sent soldiers to kill Weixue, Dong, and Regional Commander Yang Zhong at the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Ang led the personal guard straight in, killing Jiang Han and the eunuchs Li Zeng and Deng Guang at the feast, while other men were sent to kill Weixue, Dong, and Regional Commander Yang Zhong at their offices.

sentences.zh: 遂焚官府，釋囚繫，撤黃河渡船於西岸以絕渡者。

translations.literal: They then burned the government offices, released prisoners, and moved Yellow River ferry boats to the west bank to cut off crossing.
translations.idiomatic: They burned the government offices, freed the prisoners, and moved the Yellow River ferries to the west bank to block passage.

sentences.zh: 遣人招楊英、仇鉞，皆佯許之。

translations.literal: Men were sent to summon Yang Ying and Qiu Yue; both feigned agreement.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to summon Yang Ying and Qiu Yue; both pretended to comply.

sentences.zh: 英率衆保王宏堡，衆潰，英奔靈州。

translations.literal: Ying led the crowd to hold Wanghong Fort; the force collapsed and Ying fled to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying gathered his men at Wanghong Fort, but the force broke and he fled to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 鉞引還，寘鐇奪其軍，出金帛犒將士。

translations.literal: Yue turned back; Zhifan seized his army and distributed gold and silk to reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue turned back, Zhifan seized his army and handed out gold and silk to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 偽署何錦大將軍，周昂、丁廣副將軍，張欽先鋒，魏鎮、楊泰等總兵都護。

translations.literal: He falsely appointed He Jin Grand General, Zhou Ang and Ding Guang Vice Generals, Zhang Qin vanguard, and Wei Zhen, Yang Tai, and others Grand Commanders and Guardians.
translations.idiomatic: He made He Jin Grand General in name, Zhou Ang and Ding Guang Vice Generals, Zhang Qin vanguard, and Wei Zhen, Yang Tai, and others overall commanders and guardians.

sentences.zh: 令孫景文作檄，以討劉瑾為名。

translations.literal: He ordered Sun Jingwen to compose a proclamation in the name of punishing Liu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He had Sun Jingwen draft a proclamation under the banner of punishing Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 陝西總兵官曹雄聞變，遣指揮黃正駐靈州，檄楊英督靈州兵防黃河。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Commander-in-Chief Cao Xiong, hearing of the uprising, sent Commander Huang Zheng to hold Lingzhou and ordered Yang Ying to direct Lingzhou troops to guard the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi Commander-in-Chief Cao Xiong learned of the revolt, he sent Commander Huang Zheng to hold Lingzhou and ordered Yang Ying to deploy Lingzhou troops along the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 都指揮韓斌、總兵官侯勳、參將時源各以兵會。

translations.literal: Regional Commanders Han Bin and Hou Xun and Regional Commander Shi Yuan each came with troops to join.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commanders Han Bin and Hou Xun and Regional Commander Shi Yuan each marched in with their forces.

sentences.zh: 英密使蒼頭報仇鉞為內應，令史墉浮渡奪西岸船，營河東，焚大、小二壩草。

translations.literal: Ying secretly sent a servant to tell Qiu Yue to act as an inside collaborator, and ordered Shi Yong to swim across, seize the west-bank boats, encamp east of the river, and burn the grass at the Great and Small Dams.
translations.idiomatic: Ying secretly sent a servant to Qiu Yue to serve as an inside collaborator, and ordered Shi Yong to swim the river, seize the west-bank boats, camp on the east bank, and burn the fodder at the Great and Small Dams.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇懼，令錦等出禦，獨留昂守城，使使召鉞。

translations.literal: Zhifan grew afraid and ordered Jin and the others out to meet the attack, keeping Ang alone to hold the city, and sent a messenger to summon Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Zhifan sent Jin and the others out to fight while leaving Ang to hold the city, and dispatched a messenger to summon Yue.

sentences.zh: 鉞稱病，昂來問疾，鉞刺昂死。

translations.literal: Yue claimed illness; when Ang came to inquire after his health, Yue stabbed him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yue feigned illness; when Ang came to visit him, Yue stabbed him dead.

sentences.zh: 令親兵馳寘鐇第，擊殺景文、連等十餘人，遂禽寘鐇，迎英衆入。

translations.literal: He ordered his personal guard to gallop to Zhifan's residence, strike down Jingwen, Lian, and more than ten others, then seize Zhifan and welcome Ying's force into the city.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his personal guard racing to Zhifan's residence, cut down Jingwen, Lian, and more than ten others, seized Zhifan, and admitted Ying's troops.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇反十有八日而禽。

translations.literal: Zhifan's rebellion lasted eighteen days before he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifan's rebellion lasted only eighteen days before he was taken.

sentences.zh: 錦、廣、泰、欽先後皆獲，械送伏誅。

translations.literal: Jin, Guang, Tai, and Qin were captured one after another, sent under guard, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Guang, Tai, and Qin were captured in turn, sent under guard, and put to death.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇賜死，諸子弟皆論死。

translations.literal: Zhifan was granted death; all his sons and younger brothers were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifan was granted death by the emperor's command; all his sons and younger brothers were condemned to die.

sentences.zh: 有孫鼒材逃出，削髮為僧，居永寧山中。

translations.literal: A grandson, Zicai, escaped, shaved his head, and became a monk, living in the Yongning mountains.
translations.idiomatic: One grandson, Zicai, escaped, took monastic vows, and lived in the Yongning mountains.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為土僧所凌，詣官言狀。

translations.literal: Before long he was bullied by local monks and went to the magistrate to report his case.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was harassed by local monks and went to the magistrate to state his grievance.

sentences.zh: 傳至京，安化宮人左寶瓶在浣衣局，使驗之，咤曰：「此鼒材殿下也。

translations.literal: When the report reached the capital, Zuobaoping, a palace woman of Anhua in the Laundry Bureau, was sent to identify him; she exclaimed, "This is His Highness Zicai."
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the capital, Zuobaoping, a woman of the Anhua palace household in the Laundry Bureau, was sent to identify him; she cried out, "This is His Highness Zicai!"

sentences.zh: 」帝念其自歸，免死。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that he had surrendered of his own accord, spared his life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, taking account of his voluntary surrender, spared his life.

sentences.zh: 安置鳳陽。

translations.literal: He was settled at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was resettled at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 寧獻王權，太祖第十七子。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Ning, Quan, was the seventeenth son of the Taizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Ning, Quan, was the Taizu Emperor's seventeenth son.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十四年封。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He received his princely title in the twenty-fourth year of the Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 踰二年，就藩大寧。

translations.literal: Two years later he went to establish his princely court at Dening.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he took up his fief at Dening.
