sentences.zh: 大寧在喜峯口外，古會州地，東連遼左，西接宣府，為巨鎮。

translations.literal: Dening lay beyond Xifeng Pass in the old territory of Huizhou, linked to Liaodong in the east and Xuanfu in the west—a great strategic stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Dening stood beyond Xifeng Pass in the old lands of Huizhou, linked east to Liaodong and west to Xuanfu—a major strategic bastion.

sentences.zh: 帶甲八萬，革車六千，所屬朶顏三衞騎兵皆驍勇善戰。

translations.literal: It fielded eighty thousand armored troops and six thousand war chariots; the cavalry of the three guards of Duoyan under its command were all fierce and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Its armored force numbered eighty thousand with six thousand war chariots, and the cavalry of the three Duoyan guards under its command were all fierce fighters.

sentences.zh: 權數會諸王出塞，以善謀稱。

translations.literal: Quan repeatedly joined the other princes in campaigns beyond the frontier and was known for shrewd planning.
translations.idiomatic: Quan often joined the other princes on campaigns beyond the frontier and was famed for shrewd counsel.

sentences.zh: 燕王初起兵，與諸將議曰：「曩余巡塞上，見大寧諸軍慓悍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan first raised troops, he said in council with his generals: "Formerly when I toured the frontier I saw how fierce the armies of Dening were."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan first took up arms, he told his generals in council: "When I toured the frontier I saw how formidable Dening's armies were."

sentences.zh: 吾得大寧，斷遼東，取邊騎助戰，大事濟矣。

translations.literal: "If I obtain Dening, cut off Liaodong, and take the frontier cavalry to aid the war, the great enterprise will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: "If I gain Dening, sever Liaodong, and enlist the frontier cavalry, the great enterprise will succeed."

sentences.zh: 」建文元年，朝議恐權與燕合，使人召權，權不至，坐削三護衞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen the court, fearing Quan would join the Yan cause, sent men to summon him; he did not come and was punished by the stripping of his three guard units.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwen the court, fearing Quan would side with the Prince of Yan, summoned him; he refused to come and was stripped of his three guard units.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，江陰侯吳高攻永平，燕王往救。

translations.literal: That year, in the ninth month, Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao attacked Yongping and the Prince of Yan went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao attacked Yongping, and the Prince of Yan marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 高退，燕王遂自劉家口間道趨大寧，詭言窮蹙來求救。

translations.literal: When Gao withdrew, the Prince of Yan took a secret route through Liujiakou toward Dening, falsely claiming he was in desperate straits and had come to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao withdrew, the Prince of Yan slipped through Liujiakou toward Dening, claiming in feigned distress that he had come to beg for help.

sentences.zh: 權邀燕王單騎入城，執手大慟，具言不得已起兵故，求代草表謝罪。

translations.literal: Quan invited the Prince of Yan to enter the city alone on horseback; they clasped hands and wept greatly, and Quan fully explained why he had been forced to raise troops and asked him to draft a memorial of apology on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Quan invited the Prince of Yan to ride into the city alone; they clasped hands and wept, and Quan explained at length why he had been forced to rebel and asked him to draft a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 居數日，欵洽不為備。

translations.literal: After several days of warm fellowship he was off his guard.
translations.idiomatic: After several days of cordial intimacy he lowered his guard.

sentences.zh: 北平銳卒伏城外，吏士稍稍入城，陰結三衞部長及諸戍卒。

translations.literal: Beiping's picked soldiers lay hidden outside the walls; officers and clerks gradually entered the city and secretly won over the chiefs of the three guards and the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Beiping's elite troops lay hidden outside the walls while officers and clerks slipped into the city and secretly won over the chiefs of the three guards and the garrison soldiers.

sentences.zh: 燕王辭去，權祖之郊，伏兵起，擁權行。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan took his leave, Quan escorted him to the suburbs; hidden troops rose up and seized Quan as he went.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Yan departed, Quan saw him off to the suburbs; ambushers sprang up and seized him on the road.

sentences.zh: 三衞彍騎及諸戍卒，一呼畢集。

translations.literal: The Mongol cavalry of the three guards and the garrison troops answered one call and all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol cavalry of the three guards and all the garrison troops rallied at a single summons.

sentences.zh: 守將朱鑑不能禦，戰歿。

translations.literal: The defending commander Zhu Jian could not hold them off and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Defending commander Zhu Jian could not repel them and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 王府妃妾世子皆隨入松亭關，歸北平，大寧城為空。

translations.literal: The prince's consorts, concubines, and heir all followed through Songting Pass back to Beiping; Dening city was left empty.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's consorts, concubines, and heir all passed through Songting Pass back to Beiping, and Dening was left empty.

sentences.zh: 權入燕軍，時時為燕王草檄。

translations.literal: Quan entered the Yan army and from time to time drafted proclamations for the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan joined the Yan army and from time to time drafted proclamations for the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕王謂權，事成，當中分天下。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan told Quan that when success was achieved they would divide the realm between them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan promised Quan that when the enterprise succeeded they would divide the realm between them.

sentences.zh: 比即位，王乞改南土。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan acceded to the throne, the prince begged to be moved to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, the Prince of Yan acceded; Quan begged to be transferred to the south.

sentences.zh: 請蘇州，曰：「畿內也。

translations.literal: He asked for Suzhou, saying, "It is within the metropolitan region."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for Suzhou, saying, "It lies within the metropolitan region."

sentences.zh: 」請錢塘，曰：「皇考以予五弟，竟不果。

translations.literal: He asked for Qiantang, saying, "Our late father meant it for his fifth son, but it never came to pass."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for Qiantang, saying, "Our late father had meant it for his fifth son, yet it never came to pass."

sentences.zh: 建文無道，以王其弟，亦不克享。

translations.literal: "Jianwen was without the Way; though he would have enfeoffed me as his younger brother, I could not enjoy it either."
translations.idiomatic: "Jianwen was without the Way; even had he enfeoffed me as his younger brother, I could not have enjoyed it."

sentences.zh: 建寧、重慶、荊州、東昌皆善地，惟弟擇焉。」

translations.literal: "Jianning, Chongqing, Jingzhou, and Dongchang are all fine places—let my younger brother choose among them."
translations.idiomatic: "Jianning, Chongqing, Jingzhou, and Dongchang are all fine places—let my younger brother choose."

sentences.zh: 永樂元年二月改封南昌，帝親製詩送之，詔即布政司為邸，瓴甋規制無所更。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yongle he was reassigned to Nanchang; the emperor personally composed a poem to send him off and ordered the princely residence set up in the provincial administration compound without altering its tile-and-brick scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yongle's first year he was reassigned to Nanchang; the Chengzu Emperor composed a poem to send him off and ordered his residence established in the provincial administration compound, its scale of tile and brick unchanged.

sentences.zh: 已而人告權巫蠱誹謗事，密探無驗，得已。

translations.literal: Soon afterward someone reported Quan for witchcraft and slander; secret investigation found no proof, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone accused Quan of witchcraft and slander; secret investigation found nothing, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 自是日韜晦，搆精廬一區，鼓琴讀書其間，終成祖世得無患。

translations.literal: From then on he kept a low profile day by day, built a secluded study, and played the zither and read books there; through the Chengzu reign he escaped trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he kept a low profile, built a secluded study where he played the zither and read, and passed the Chengzu reign without incident.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，法禁稍解，乃上書言南昌非其封國。

translations.literal: In the Renzong reign, when legal restrictions were somewhat relaxed, he submitted a memorial saying Nanchang was not his allotted fief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renzong reign, when legal restrictions eased somewhat, he memorialized that Nanchang was not his allotted fief.

sentences.zh: 帝答書曰：「南昌，叔父受之皇考已二十餘年，非封國而何？

translations.literal: The emperor replied in writing: "Nanchang—Uncle, you have held it from our late father for more than twenty years; if it is not a fief, what is it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote back: "Uncle, you have held Nanchang from our late father for more than twenty years—if that is not a fief, what is?"

sentences.zh: 」宣德三年請乞近郭灌城鄉土田。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he requested suburban farmland at Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande he petitioned for suburban farmland at Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 明年又論宗室不應定品級。

translations.literal: The next year he again argued that members of the imperial clan should not be assigned fixed rank grades.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again argued that members of the imperial clan ought not be assigned fixed rank grades.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，頗有所詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 權上書謝過。

translations.literal: Quan submitted a memorial apologizing for his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Quan submitted a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 時年已老，有司多齮齕以示威重。

translations.literal: By then he was already old, and local officials often picked at him to show their authority.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was already old, and local officials often found fault with him to assert their authority.

sentences.zh: 權日與文學士相往還，託志翀舉，自號臞仙。

translations.literal: Quan associated daily with literary scholars, feigning disinterest in office, and styled himself the Emaciated Immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Quan spent his days among literary scholars, affecting disinterest in office, and styled himself the Emaciated Immortal.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉敕輯通鑑博論二卷，又作家訓六篇，寧國儀範七十四章，漢唐祕史二卷，史斷一卷，文譜八卷，詩譜一卷，其他註纂數十種。

translations.literal: He once received an imperial order to compile Broad Discussions on the Comprehensive Mirror in two juan, and also wrote Family Instructions in six sections, Ceremonial Standards of the Ning Principality in seventy-four chapters, Secret Histories of Han and Tang in two juan, Judgments on History in one juan, Literary Patterns in eight juan, Poetic Patterns in one juan, and several dozen other annotated compilations.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial command he compiled Broad Discussions on the Comprehensive Mirror in two juan, and also wrote Family Instructions in six sections, Ceremonial Standards of the Ning Principality in seventy-four chapters, Secret Histories of Han and Tang in two juan, Judgments on History in one juan, Literary Patterns in eight juan, Poetic Patterns in one juan, and dozens of other annotated works.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 世子盤烒先卒，孫靖王奠培嗣。

translations.literal: The heir Panlie died first; the grandson Prince Jing Dianpei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Panlie died first; his grandson Prince Jing Dianpei succeeded.

sentences.zh: 奠培善文辭，而性卞急，多嫌猜。

translations.literal: Dianpei was skilled in literary composition but by nature irascible and given to much suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Dianpei wrote well but was quick-tempered and deeply suspicious.

sentences.zh: 景泰七年，弟弋陽王奠壏訐其反逆，巡撫韓雍以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jingtai his younger brother Prince of Yiyang Dianjian denounced him for treason, and Grand Coordinator Han Yong reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jingtai his younger brother Prince of Yiyang Dianjian accused him of treason, and Grand Coordinator Han Yong reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝遣官往讞，不實。

translations.literal: The emperor sent officials to investigate; it was not true.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent officials to investigate; the charge proved false.

sentences.zh: 時軍民連逮者六七百人，會英宗復辟，俱赦釋，惟謫戍其教授游堅。

translations.literal: At the time six or seven hundred soldiers and civilians had been implicated; when the Yingzong Emperor regained the throne all were pardoned and released, save that his instructor You Jian was banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven hundred soldiers and civilians had been implicated; when the Yingzong Emperor regained the throne all were pardoned, though his instructor You Jian was banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 奠培由是憾守土官，不為禮。

translations.literal: Dianpei therefore resented the local officials and refused them courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Dianpei therefore bore a grudge against the local officials and withheld courtesy from them.

sentences.zh: 布政使崔恭積不平，王府事多持不行。

translations.literal: Administrative Commissioner Cui Gong nursed longstanding grievances, and many matters of the princely household were blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative Commissioner Cui Gong had long nursed grievances, and many princely household matters were blocked.

sentences.zh: 奠培遂劾奏恭不法。

translations.literal: Dianpei then memorialized accusing Gong of unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Dianpei then memorialized accusing Gong of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 恭與按察使原傑亦奏奠培私獻、惠二王宮人，逼內官熊璧自盡。

translations.literal: Gong and Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Jie also memorialized that Dianpei had privately presented palace women to the Princes of Xian and Hui and had driven the inner attendant Xiong Bi to suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Surveillance Commissioner Yuan Jie also reported that Dianpei had privately presented palace women to the Princes of Xian and Hui and had driven inner attendant Xiong Bi to suicide.

sentences.zh: 按問皆實，遂奪護衞。

translations.literal: Investigation confirmed all charges, and his guard unit was then stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed every charge, and his guard unit was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 踰三年，而奠壏以有罪賜死。

translations.literal: More than three years later Dianjian was granted death for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years later Dianjian was granted death for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 初，錦衣衞指揮逯杲聽詗事者言，誣奠壏烝母。

translations.literal: At first, Brocade Guard Commander Lu Gao, heeding informants, falsely accused Dianjian of committing incest with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At first Brocade Guard Commander Lu Gao, heeding informants, falsely accused Dianjian of incest with his mother.

sentences.zh: 帝令奠培具實以聞，復遣駙馬都尉薛桓與杲按問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Dianpei to report the facts and again sent Chief Commandant of Imperial Son-in-Law Xue Huan with Gao to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Dianpei to report the facts and again sent Chief Commandant of Imperial Son-in-Law Xue Huan with Gao to investigate.

sentences.zh: 奠培奏無是事，杲按亦無實。

translations.literal: Dianpei memorialized that there was no such matter, and Gao's investigation likewise found no proof.
translations.idiomatic: Dianpei memorialized that no such thing had occurred, and Gao's investigation also found nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責問杲。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and sharply questioned Gao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and sharply rebuked Gao.

sentences.zh: 杲懼，仍以為實，遂賜奠壏母子自盡，焚其屍。

translations.literal: Gao grew afraid and still treated it as true; Dianjian and his mother were then granted death by their own hand, and their corpses were burned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, in fear, still upheld the charge as true; Dianjian and his mother were granted death by their own hand and their bodies burned.

sentences.zh: 是日雷雨大作，平地水深數尺，衆咸冤之。

translations.literal: That day thunder and rain burst forth and water on level ground stood several chi deep; all deemed it a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: That day thunder and rain erupted and water on level ground stood several chi deep; all regarded it as a grievous injustice.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，奠培薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi Dianpei died.
translations.idiomatic: Dianpei died in the fourth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 子康王覲鈞嗣，十年薨。

translations.literal: His son Prince Kang Jingjun succeeded and died in the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Prince Kang Jingjun succeeded and died in the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 子上高王宸濠嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chenhao, Prince of Shanggao, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chenhao, Prince of Shanggao, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 其母，故娼也。

translations.literal: His mother had once been a courtesan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had once been a courtesan.

sentences.zh: 始生，靖王夢蛇啖其室，旦日鴟鳴，惡之。

translations.literal: At his birth the Prince of Jing dreamed a snake devoured his chamber; the next morning an owl cried, and he regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth the Prince of Jing dreamed a snake devoured his chamber; when an owl cried at dawn he took it as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 及長，輕佻無威儀，而善以文行自飾。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was frivolous and without dignified bearing, yet skilled at cloaking himself in literary conduct.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he was frivolous and lacked dignified bearing, yet knew how to cloak himself in literary propriety.

sentences.zh: 術士李自然、李日芳妄言其有異表，又謂城東南有天子氣。

translations.literal: The diviners Li Ziran and Li Rifang falsely said he bore an extraordinary countenance, and also said there was an emperor's aura southeast of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The diviners Li Ziran and Li Rifang falsely declared he bore an extraordinary countenance and claimed an emperor's aura lay southeast of the city.

sentences.zh: 宸濠喜，時時詗中朝事，聞謗言輒喜。

translations.literal: Chenhao rejoiced and constantly inquired into affairs at court; whenever he heard slanderous talk he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao was delighted and constantly spied on court affairs; slanderous talk always pleased him.

sentences.zh: 或言帝明聖，朝廷治，即怒。

translations.literal: If anyone said the emperor was wise and sagely and the court well governed, he grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone praised the emperor as wise and the court as well governed, he flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 武宗末年無子，羣臣數請召宗室子子之。

translations.literal: In the late Wuzong reign the emperor had no son, and the ministers repeatedly asked that a clansman's son be summoned to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Wuzong reign the emperor had no heir, and ministers repeatedly asked that a clansman's son be summoned to succeed.

sentences.zh: 宸濠屬疎，顧深結左右，於帝前稱其賢。

translations.literal: Chenhao stood far in the succession, yet he deeply cultivated those close to the emperor and had them praise his worth before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao stood far from the succession, yet he cultivated the emperor's intimates and had them praise his virtues at court.

sentences.zh: 初，宸濠賄劉瑾，復所奪護衞。

translations.literal: At first Chenhao bribed Liu Jin and recovered his stripped guard unit.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chenhao bribed Liu Jin and regained his stripped guard unit.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，仍論奪。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed it was again ordered stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed the guard unit was stripped away again.

sentences.zh: 及陸完為兵部尚書，宸濠結嬖人錢寧、臧賢為內主，欲奏復，大學士費宏執不可。

translations.literal: When Lu Wan became Minister of War, Chenhao cultivated the favorites Qian Ning and Zang Xian as inside backers and sought a memorial for restoration; Grand Secretary Fei Hong insisted it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Wan became Minister of War, Chenhao won over the favorites Qian Ning and Zang Xian as inside backers and sought restoration of the guard unit; Grand Secretary Fei Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 諸嬖人乘宏讀廷試卷，取中旨行之。

translations.literal: The favorites, while Hong was reading palace examination papers, took a secret edict and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The favorites, while Hong was reading palace examination papers, seized a secret edict and had it executed.

sentences.zh: 宸濠益恣，擅殺都指揮戴宣，逐布政使鄭岳、御史范輅，幽知府鄭巘、宋以方。

translations.literal: Chenhao grew all the more unrestrained: he killed Regional Commander Dai Xuan on his own authority, drove out Administrative Commissioners Zheng Yue and Censor Fan Luo, and imprisoned Prefects Zheng Yan and Song Yifang.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao grew bolder still: he killed Regional Commander Dai Xuan on his own authority, drove out Administrative Commissioner Zheng Yue and Censor Fan Luo, and imprisoned Prefects Zheng Yan and Song Yifang.

sentences.zh: 盡奪諸附王府民廬，責民間子錢，強奪田宅子女，養羣盜，劫財江、湖間，有司不敢問。

translations.literal: He seized all dwellings of subjects attached to the princely house, exacted usurious loans from the people, forcibly seized fields, houses, sons, and daughters, kept bands of robbers, and plundered wealth on the rivers and lakes; local officials dared not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He seized every dwelling of subjects tied to the princely house, exacted usurious loans, forcibly took fields, houses, children, and wives, maintained bands of robbers, and plundered on the rivers and lakes while local officials dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 日與致仕都御史李士實、舉人劉養正等謀不軌。

translations.literal: Day and night he plotted treason with retired Censor-in-Chief Li Shishi and Presented Scholar Liu Yangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he plotted rebellion with retired Censor-in-Chief Li Shishi and Presented Scholar Liu Yangzheng.

sentences.zh: 副使胡世寧請朝廷早裁抑之。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Hu Shining asked the court to restrain him early.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Hu Shining asked the court to curb him early.

sentences.zh: 宸濠連奏世寧罪，世寧坐謫戍，自是無敢言者。

translations.literal: Chenhao repeatedly memorialized Shining's crimes; Shining was banished to frontier service, and from then on none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao repeatedly memorialized against Shining; Shining was banished to frontier service, and thereafter none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年，典儀閻順，內官陳宣、劉良間行詣闕上變。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde Ceremonial Director Yan Shun and inner attendants Chen Xuan and Liu Liang secretly went to the capital to report the plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhengde Ceremonial Director Yan Shun and inner attendants Chen Xuan and Liu Liang secretly went to the capital to report the plot.

sentences.zh: 寧、賢等庇之，不問。

translations.literal: Ning and Xian and the others shielded him, and no inquiry was made.
translations.idiomatic: Ning and Xian shielded him, and no inquiry followed.

sentences.zh: 宸濠疑出承奉周儀，殺儀家及典仗查武等數百人。

translations.literal: Chenhao suspected the leak came from palace attendant Zhou Yi and killed Yi's family and Ceremonial Guard Cha Wu and several hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao suspected palace attendant Zhou Yi of the leak and killed Yi's family along with Ceremonial Guard Cha Wu and several hundred others.

sentences.zh: 巡撫都御史孫燧列其事，中道為所邀，不得達。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Sun Sui listed the matter in a memorial but was intercepted on the road and could not deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Sun Sui memorialized the affair, but was intercepted on the road and could not deliver it.

sentences.zh: 宸濠又賄錢寧，求取中旨，召其子司香太廟。

translations.literal: Chenhao again bribed Qian Ning to obtain a secret edict summoning his son to attend incense at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao again bribed Qian Ning to obtain a secret edict summoning his son to perform incense at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 寧言於帝，用異色龍牋，加金報賜。

translations.literal: Ning spoke to the emperor, and a dragon-letter of unusual color with gold added was bestowed in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ning spoke to the emperor, and in reply a dragon-letter of unusual color with gold added was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 異色龍牋者，故事所賜監國書牋也。

translations.literal: A dragon-letter of unusual color was, by precedent, what was granted for regency documents.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent a dragon-letter of unusual color was granted for regency documents.

sentences.zh: 宸濠大喜，列仗受賀。

translations.literal: Chenhao rejoiced greatly and lined up his guard to receive congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao was overjoyed and lined up his guard to receive congratulations.

sentences.zh: 復勒諸生、父老奏闕下，稱其孝且勤。

translations.literal: He again compelled students and elders to memorialize at court praising his filial piety and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: He again forced students and village elders to memorialize at court praising his filial piety and diligence.

sentences.zh: 時邊將江彬新得幸，太監張忠附彬，欲傾寧、賢，乘間為帝言：「寧、賢盛稱寧王，陛下以為何如？

translations.literal: At the time the frontier general Jiang Bin had newly won favor; eunuch Zhang Zhong attached himself to Bin and, wishing to topple Ning and Xian, seized an opportunity to tell the emperor: "Ning and Xian lavishly praise the Prince of Ning—what does Your Majesty think of that?"
translations.idiomatic: Frontier general Jiang Bin had newly won favor; eunuch Zhang Zhong attached himself to Bin and, seeking to topple Ning and Xian, told the emperor: "Ning and Xian lavishly praise the Prince of Ning—what does Your Majesty make of that?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「薦文武百執事，可任使也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "To recommend civil and military officials fit for service is one thing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Recommending civil and military officials fit for office is one thing."

sentences.zh: 薦藩王何為者？

translations.literal: "Why recommend a prince of the blood?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why recommend a prince of the blood?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「賢稱寧王孝，譏陛下不孝耳。

translations.literal: Zhong said, "Xian praises the Prince of Ning's filial piety—he is mocking Your Majesty's lack of filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "When Xian praises the Prince of Ning's filial piety, he mocks Your Majesty as unfilial."

sentences.zh: 稱寧王勤，譏陛下不勤耳。

translations.literal: "He praises the Prince of Ning's diligence—he is mocking Your Majesty's lack of diligence."
translations.idiomatic: "When he praises the Prince of Ning's diligence, he mocks Your Majesty as idle."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Just so."

sentences.zh: 」下詔逐王府人，毋留闕下。

translations.literal: An edict was issued expelling men of the princely house and forbidding them to remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict expelled men of the princely house and forbade them to remain at court.

sentences.zh: 是時宸濠與士實、養正日夜謀，益遣姦人盧孔章等分布水陸孔道，萬里傳報，浹旬往返，蹤跡大露，朝野皆知其必反。

translations.literal: At that time Chenhao, with Shishi and Yangzheng, plotted day and night, and increasingly sent agents such as Lu Kongzhang to spread along land and water routes; reports traveled ten thousand li and returned within ten days—the trail was fully exposed, and court and country all knew he would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chenhao plotted day and night with Shishi and Yangzheng, dispatching agents such as Lu Kongzhang along every land and water route; messages crossed ten thousand li and returned within ten days—the trail lay fully exposed, and all knew he would rebel.

sentences.zh: 巡撫都御史孫燧七上章言之，皆為所邀沮。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Sun Sui memorialized seven times, but each time was intercepted and blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Sun Sui memorialized seven times, yet each memorial was intercepted.

sentences.zh: 諸權姦多得宸濠金錢，匿其事不以聞。

translations.literal: Many powerful favorites had received Chenhao's gold and silver and concealed the matter without reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: Many powerful favorites had taken Chenhao's gold and silver and concealed the affair.

sentences.zh: 十四年，御史蕭淮疏言宸濠諸罪，謂不早制，將來之患有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Censor Xiao Huai memorialized Chenhao's crimes, saying that if he were not restrained early the future harm would be beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Censor Xiao Huai memorialized Chenhao's crimes, warning that unless he was restrained early the harm to come would be beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 疏下內閣，大學士楊廷和謂宜如宣宗處趙府事，遣勳戚大臣宣諭，令王自新。

translations.literal: The memorial went to the Grand Secretariat; Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe said it should be handled as the Xuande Emperor had handled the Zhao principality affair—send a meritorious minister of the imperial clan to announce the edict and bid the prince reform.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the Grand Secretariat; Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe argued it should be handled as the Xuande Emperor had handled the Zhao affair—send a meritorious imperial clansman to announce the edict and bid the prince reform.

sentences.zh: 帝命駙馬都尉崔元、都御史顏頤壽、太監賴義持諭往，收其護衞，令還所奪官民田。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chief Commandant of Imperial Son-in-Law Cui Yuan, Censor-in-Chief Yan Shoushou, and eunuch Lai Yi to go bearing the announcement, strip his guard unit, and order the return of seized official and private fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chief Commandant of Imperial Son-in-Law Cui Yuan, Censor-in-Chief Yan Shoushou, and eunuch Lai Yi to announce the edict, strip his guard unit, and order return of seized official and private lands.

sentences.zh: 宸濠聞元等且至，乃定計，以己生辰日宴諸守土官。

translations.literal: When Chenhao heard Yuan and the others were about to arrive, he settled on a plan to feast the local officials on his birthday.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yuan and the others were approaching, Chenhao decided to feast the local officials on his birthday.

sentences.zh: 詰旦皆入謝。

translations.literal: At dawn they all came to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they all came to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 宸濠命甲士環之，稱奉太后密旨，令起兵入朝。

translations.literal: Chenhao had armored soldiers surround them, claiming a secret edict from the Empress Dowager ordering them to raise troops and enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao had armored soldiers surround them, claiming a secret edict from the Empress Dowager ordering them to raise troops and march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 孫燧及副使許逵不從，縛出斬之。

translations.literal: Sun Sui and Vice Commissioner Xu Kui refused; they were bound and led out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sui and Vice Commissioner Xu Kui refused; they were bound, led out, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 執御史王金，主事馬思聰、金山，參議黃宏、許傚廉，布政使胡廉，參政陳杲、劉棐，僉事賴鳳，指揮許金、白昂等下獄。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Jin, Section Head Ma Sicong and Jin Shan, Administrative Commissioner Hu Lian, Participating Administrators Chen Guo and Liu Fei, Vice Commissioners Lai Feng, Commanders Xu Jin and Bai Ang, and others were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jin, Section Heads Ma Sicong and Jin Shan, Administrative Commissioner Hu Lian, Participating Administrators Chen Guo and Liu Fei, Vice Commissioner Lai Feng, and Commanders Xu Jin and Bai Ang were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 參政王綸、季斆，僉事潘鵬、師夔，布政使梁宸，按察使楊璋，副使唐錦皆從逆。

translations.literal: Participating Administrator Wang Lun and Ji Xiao, Vice Commissioners Pan Peng and Shi Kui, Administrative Commissioner Liang Chen, Surveillance Commissioner Yang Zhang, and Vice Commissioner Tang Jin all followed the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Administrators Wang Lun and Ji Xiao, Vice Commissioners Pan Peng and Shi Kui, Administrative Commissioner Liang Chen, Surveillance Commissioner Yang Zhang, and Vice Commissioner Tang Jin all joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以李士實、劉養正為左、右丞相，王綸為兵部尚書，集兵號十萬。

translations.literal: Li Shishi and Liu Yangzheng were made Left and Right Grand Chancellors, Wang Lun Minister of War, and troops were gathered numbering one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shishi and Liu Yangzheng were made Left and Right Grand Chancellors, Wang Lun Minister of War, and one hundred thousand troops were mustered.

sentences.zh: 命其承奉涂欽與素所蓄羣盜閔念四等，略九江、南康，破之。

translations.literal: He ordered his palace attendant Tu Qin and the robbers he had long kept, such as Min Niansi, to overrun Jiujiang and Nankang and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered palace attendant Tu Qin and longtime robber retainers such as Min Niansi to overrun Jiujiang and Nankang.

sentences.zh: 馳檄指斥朝廷。

translations.literal: He sent out proclamations denouncing the court.
translations.idiomatic: He issued proclamations denouncing the court.

sentences.zh: 七月壬辰朔，宸濠出江西，留其黨宜春王拱樤、內官萬銳等守城，自帥舟師蔽江下，攻安慶。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, renchen, Chenhao left Jiangxi, leaving his partisans Prince of Yichun Gong Suo, eunuch Wan Rui, and others to hold the city; he himself led a fleet covering the river downstream to attack Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the first day of the seventh month, Chenhao left Jiangxi, leaving partisans Prince of Yichun Gong Suo, eunuch Wan Rui, and others to hold the city while he led a fleet downriver to attack Anqing.

sentences.zh: 汀贛巡撫僉都御史王守仁聞變，與吉安知府伍文定等檄諸郡兵先後至。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator and Vice Censor-in-Chief of Ting-Gan Wang Shouren, hearing of the uprising, with Ji'an Prefect Wu Wendin and others issued orders and troops from the various prefectures arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Shouren of Ting-Gan, hearing of the revolt, with Ji'an Prefect Wu Wendin and others summoned troops from the prefectures, which arrived in succession.

sentences.zh: 乃使奉新知縣劉守緒破其墳廠伏兵。

translations.literal: He then had Fengxin Magistrate Liu Shouxu break the ambush at the tomb factory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fengxin Magistrate Liu Shouxu to break the ambush at the tomb factory.

sentences.zh: 戊申，直攻南昌。

translations.literal: On wushen he attacked Nanchang directly.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen he struck directly at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，城破，拱樤、銳等皆就禽，宮人自焚死。

translations.literal: On xinhai the city fell; Gong Suo, Rui, and the others were all captured, and palace women burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the city fell; Gong Suo, Rui, and the others were captured, and palace women burned themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 宸濠方攻安慶不克，聞南昌破，大恐，解圍還，守仁逆擊之。

translations.literal: Chenhao was attacking Anqing without success when he heard Nanchang had fallen; greatly afraid, he lifted the siege and returned, and Shouren met him with a counterattack.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao was failing to take Anqing when he learned Nanchang had fallen; in terror he lifted the siege and turned back, and Shouren struck him on the retreat.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，遇於黃家渡，賊兵乘風進薄，氣驕甚。

translations.literal: On yimao they met at Huangjiadu; the rebel troops, riding the wind, pressed forward closely and were very arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao they met at Huangjiadu; the rebels, riding a favorable wind, pressed close and fought with great arrogance.

sentences.zh: 文定及指揮余恩佯北，誘賊趨利，前後不相及。

translations.literal: Wendin and Commander Yu En feigned retreat, luring the rebels to chase gain so that front and rear could not keep contact.
translations.idiomatic: Wendin and Commander Yu En feigned retreat, luring the rebels to chase profit until front and rear lost contact.

sentences.zh: 知府邢珣、徐璉、戴德孺從後急擊，文定帥還兵乘之，賊潰，斬溺萬計。

translations.literal: Prefects Xing Qi, Xu Lian, and Dai Deru struck hard from the rear; Wendin turned his force and pressed the attack, and the rebels collapsed—those cut down or drowned numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects Xing Qi, Xu Lian, and Dai Deru struck from the rear; Wendin wheeled about and pressed the attack, and the rebels broke—tens of thousands were cut down or drowned.

sentences.zh: 又別遣知府陳槐、林瑊、曾璵、周朝佐復九江、南康。

translations.literal: He separately sent Prefects Chen Huai, Lin Jian, Zeng Yu, and Zhou Chaozuo to recover Jiujiang and Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Prefects Chen Huai, Lin Jian, Zeng Yu, and Zhou Chaozuo to recover Jiujiang and Nankang.

sentences.zh: 明日，復戰，官兵稍却，文定帥士卒殊死鬬，禽斬二千餘級，宸濠乃退保樵舍。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; the government troops fell back slightly, but Wendin led the soldiers in a desperate fight and captured or killed more than two thousand; Chenhao then withdrew to hold Qiaoshe.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again; government troops gave ground, but Wendin led his men in a desperate fight, capturing or killing more than two thousand, and Chenhao withdrew to Qiaoshe.

sentences.zh: 明日，官軍以火攻之，宸濠大敗。

translations.literal: The next day the government army attacked with fire; Chenhao suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the government army attacked with fire and Chenhao suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 諸妃嬪皆赴水死，將士焚溺死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: All consorts and concubines threw themselves into the water and died; soldiers burned or drowned numbered more than thirty thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and concubines drowned themselves; more than thirty thousand soldiers died by fire or water.

sentences.zh: 宸濠及其世子、郡王、儀賓並李士實、劉養正、涂欽、王綸等俱就禽。

translations.literal: Chenhao and his heir, commandery princes, imperial sons-in-law, and Li Shishi, Liu Yangzheng, Tu Qin, Wang Lun, and the others were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao, his heir, commandery princes, imperial sons-in-law, and Li Shishi, Liu Yangzheng, Tu Qin, Wang Lun, and the others were all taken.

sentences.zh: 宸濠自舉事至敗，蓋四十有三日。

translations.literal: From Chenhao's rising to his defeat, it was forty-three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: From rising to defeat, Chenhao's rebellion lasted forty-three days.

sentences.zh: 時帝聞宸濠反，下詔暴其罪，告宗廟，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard Chenhao had rebelled, he issued an edict exposing his crimes, reported to the ancestral temple, and degraded him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned Chenhao had rebelled, he issued an edict exposing his crimes, reported to the ancestral temple, and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 逮繫尚書陸完，嬖人錢寧、臧賢等，籍其家。

translations.literal: Minister Lu Wan and the favorites Qian Ning and Zang Xian were arrested and their households registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Wan and favorites Qian Ning and Zang Xian were arrested and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 江彬、張忠從臾帝親征，至良鄉，守仁捷奏至，檄止之。

translations.literal: Jiang Bin and Zhang Zhong urged the emperor to lead a campaign in person; when he reached Liangxiang, Shouren's victory memorial arrived and an order was sent to halt him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin and Zhang Zhong urged the emperor to campaign in person; at Liangxiang Shouren's victory report arrived and orders went out to stop the march.

sentences.zh: 守仁已械繫宸濠等，取道浙江。

translations.literal: Shouren had already put Chenhao and the others in fetters and took the route through Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren had already fettered Chenhao and the others and marched by way of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 帝留南京，遣許泰、朱暉及內臣張永、張忠搜捕江西餘黨，民不勝其擾。

translations.literal: The emperor remained at Nanjing and sent Xu Tai, Zhu Hui, and inner attendants Zhang Yong and Zhang Zhong to hunt down the remaining Jiangxi partisans; the people could not bear the harassment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed at Nanjing and sent Xu Tai, Zhu Hui, and inner attendants Zhang Yong and Zhang Zhong to hunt Jiangxi's remaining partisans, and the people suffered unbearably.

sentences.zh: 檄守仁還江西。

translations.literal: An order was sent for Shouren to return to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren was ordered back to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 守仁至杭州，遇張永，以俘付之，使送行在。

translations.literal: When Shouren reached Hangzhou he met Zhang Yong, handed over the captives to him, and had him escort them to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: At Hangzhou Shouren met Zhang Yong, entrusted the captives to him, and had him escort them to the temporary palace.

sentences.zh: 十五年十二月，帝受所獻俘回鑾，至通州誅之，封除。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifteenth year the emperor accepted the presented captives on his return journey and executed them at Tongzhou; the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifteenth year the emperor received the captives on his return and executed them at Tongzhou; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，宸濠謀逆，其妃婁氏嘗諫。

translations.literal: At first, when Chenhao plotted rebellion, his consort Lady Lou had admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao first plotted rebellion, his consort Lady Lou had tried to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 及敗，歎曰：「昔紂用婦言亡，我以不用婦言亡，悔何及。」

translations.literal: When he was defeated he sighed: "Formerly Zhou lost the realm through a woman's words; I lost it through not heeding a woman's words—regret comes too late."
translations.idiomatic: When defeat came he sighed: "Zhou lost the realm by heeding a woman's words; I lost it by refusing them—what use is regret now?"

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，弋陽王拱樻等言：「獻王、惠王四服子孫所共祀，非宸濠一人所自出，如臣等皆得甄別，守職業如故，而二王不獲廟享，臣竊痛之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing Prince of Yiyang Gong Su and others memorialized: "The descendants in mourning dress of the Princes Xian and Hui are jointly enshrined—they did not all spring from Chenhao alone; such as we should be sifted and allowed to keep our posts as before, yet the two princes are denied temple sacrifice—we grieve at this."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiajing Prince of Yiyang Gong Su and others memorialized: "The Princes Xian and Hui are jointly enshrined by descendants in mourning dress who did not all descend from Chenhao alone; men such as we should be sifted and continue in our posts, yet the two princes are denied temple sacrifice—we grieve at this."

sentences.zh: 」疏三上，帝命弋陽王以郡王奉祀，樂舞齋郎之屬半給之。

translations.literal: After three memorials the emperor ordered the Prince of Yiyang to perform sacrifice as a commandery prince, granting half the musicians and ritual officers.
translations.idiomatic: After three memorials the emperor ordered the Prince of Yiyang to perform sacrifice with commandery-prince standing, granting half the ritual musicians and officers.

sentences.zh: 寧藩既廢，諸郡王勢頡頏，莫能一，帝命拱樻攝府事。

translations.literal: Once the Ning principality was abolished, the commandery princes were evenly matched and none could dominate; the emperor ordered Gong Su to administer the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ning principality was abolished the commandery princes were evenly matched and none could dominate; the emperor ordered Gong Su to administer the household.

sentences.zh: 卒，樂安王拱欏攝。

translations.literal: When he died Prince of Le'an Gong Rong administered in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Prince of Le'an Gong Rong took over administration.

sentences.zh: 拱欏奏以建安、樂安、弋陽三王分治八支，著為令。

translations.literal: Gong Rong memorialized that the Princes of Jian'an, Le'an, and Yiyang should each administer one of eight branches, and this was established as a rule.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Rong memorialized that the Princes of Jian'an, Le'an, and Yiyang should each govern one of eight branches, and this was made permanent law.

sentences.zh: 石城王奠堵，惠王第四子。

translations.literal: Prince of Shicheng Moudou was the fourth son of Prince Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shicheng Moudou was the fourth son of Prince Hui.

sentences.zh: 性莊毅，家法甚嚴。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and resolute, and household discipline was very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and resolute by nature, he maintained very strict household discipline.

sentences.zh: 靖王奠培與諸郡王交惡，臨川、弋陽皆被搆得罪，奠堵獨謹約，不能坐以過失。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Dianpei was on bad terms with the commandery princes; Linchuan and Yiyang were both framed and punished, yet Moudou alone kept to propriety and could not be charged with fault.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Dianpei feuded with the commandery princes; Linchuan and Yiyang were both framed and punished, but Moudou alone kept to propriety and could not be faulted.

sentences.zh: 子覲鎬，孝友有令譽，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Jinghao was filial, friendly, and of fine reputation, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinghao was filial, affectionate, and widely esteemed, and died young.

sentences.zh: 孫宸浮嗣，與母弟宸浦、庶兄宸潣、弟宸澅皆淫縱殺人。

translations.literal: The grandson Chenfu succeeded; with his younger brother by the same mother Chenpu, elder brother by a concubine Chenxun, and younger brother Chenhui, all were licentious, unrestrained, and murderous.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Chenfu succeeded; he and his younger brother by the same mother Chenpu, elder brother by a concubine Chenxun, and younger brother Chenhui were all licentious, violent, and murderous.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年互訐奏，宸浮、宸浦並革為庶人，宸澅、宸潣奪祿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi they denounced one another in memorials; Chenfu and Chenpu were both reduced to commoners, and Chenhui and Chenxun had their stipends stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi they memorialized against one another; Chenfu and Chenpu were reduced to commoners, and Chenhui and Chenxun lost their stipends.

sentences.zh: 宸澅遂從宸濠反，雷震死。

translations.literal: Chenhui then followed Chenhao in rebellion and was killed by lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhui then joined Chenhao's rebellion and was killed by lightning.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十四年，復宸浮、宸浦冠帶，宸潣子拱梃上書為父澡雪，亦還爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiajing Chenfu and Chenpu were restored to cap and belt; Chenxun's son Gong Ting memorialized to clear his father's name, and his title was also restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiajing Chenfu and Chenpu regained cap and belt; Chenxun's son Gong Ting memorialized to clear his father's name and his title was restored as well.

sentences.zh: 宸澅弟宸浫素方正，宸濠欲屈之，不得，數使人火其居，而諷諸宗資給之以示惠，宸浫辭不受。

translations.literal: Chenhui's younger brother Chentang was by nature upright; Chenhao wished to humiliate him but could not, and repeatedly sent men to burn his dwelling while hinting to the clansmen to supply him with funds to show favor—Chentang declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhui's younger brother Chentang was upright by nature; Chenhao tried to break him but failed, repeatedly sent men to burn his house, and hinted that the clansmen should support him as a show of favor—Chentang refused.

sentences.zh: 宸濠敗，宸浫得免。

translations.literal: When Chenhao was defeated Chentang escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao fell Chentang escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 子輔國將軍拱槩，孫奉國將軍多𤎲，曾孫鎮國中尉謀㙔，三世皆端謹自好，而謀㙔尤貫串羣籍，通曉朝廷典故。

translations.literal: His son State Defender General Gong Gai, grandson State Supporter General Duoyin, and great-grandson State Defender Captain Mou Kun—three generations all upright, self-restrained, and fond of virtue—while Mou Kun especially mastered many texts and knew court precedents thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: His son State Defender General Gong Gai, grandson State Supporter General Duoyin, and great-grandson State Defender Captain Mou Kun—three generations upright and self-restrained—while Mou Kun especially mastered many texts and knew court precedent thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 諸王子孫好學敦行，自周藩中尉睦㮮而外，莫及謀㙔者。

translations.literal: Among princes' descendants who loved learning and conducted themselves well, none since Captain of the Zhou Principality Muzhen could compare with Mou Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Among princely descendants who loved learning and lived uprightly, none since Captain Muzhen of the Zhou principality could match Mou Kun.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十二年，廷議增設石城、宜春管理，命謀㙔以中尉理石城王府事，得劾治不法者。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Wanli the court debated adding Shicheng and Yichun administrations and ordered Mou Kun, as captain, to administer Shicheng princely affairs with power to impeach and punish lawbreakers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Wanli the court debated adding Shicheng and Yichun administrations and ordered Mou Kun, as captain, to administer Shicheng princely affairs with authority to impeach lawbreakers.

sentences.zh: 典藩政三十年，宗人咸就約束。

translations.literal: He managed princely affairs for thirty years, and all clansmen submitted to restraint.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years he managed princely affairs, and all clansmen submitted to discipline.

sentences.zh: 暇則閉戶讀書，著易象通、詩故、春秋戴記魯論箋及他書，凡百十有二種，皆手自繕寫。

translations.literal: In leisure he shut his door and read, composing Commentary on the Changes' Images, Old Meanings of the Odes, Lu's Recorded Discourses on the Spring and Autumn with Commentary, and other books—one hundred and twelve kinds in all, all copied by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure he shut his door to read, writing Commentary on the Changes' Images, Old Meanings of the Odes, Lu's Recorded Discourses on the Spring and Autumn with Commentary, and other works—one hundred and twelve in all, every one copied by his own hand.

sentences.zh: 黃汝亨為進賢令，投謁抗禮，劇談久之，逡巡改席。

translations.literal: Huang Yuheng was magistrate of Jinxian; Mou Kun received his visit as an equal and talked at length; after a pause he changed seats.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yuheng, magistrate of Jinxian, paid a visit; Mou Kun received him as an equal and talked at length before deferentially changing seats.

sentences.zh: 次日，北面稱弟子，人兩稱之。

translations.literal: The next day Huang faced north and called himself disciple; people praised both men.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Huang faced north and called himself disciple; both men won praise.

sentences.zh: 病革，猶與諸子說易。

translations.literal: When gravely ill he still discussed the Changes with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Even on his deathbed he discussed the Changes with his sons.

sentences.zh: 子八人，皆賢而好學。

translations.literal: He had eight sons, all worthy and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: His eight sons were all worthy and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 從弟謀㬜築室龍沙，躬耕賦詩以終。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Mou Xi built a dwelling at Longsha, farming and composing poetry to the end of his days.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Mou Xi built a house at Longsha and lived out his days farming and writing poetry.

sentences.zh: 奉國將軍拱榣，瑞昌王奠墠四世孫也。

translations.literal: State Supporter General Gong Rong was the fourth-generation descendant of Prince of Ruichang Moudian.
translations.idiomatic: State Supporter General Gong Rong was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince of Ruichang Moudian.

sentences.zh: 父宸渠為宸濠累，逮繫中都。

translations.literal: His father Chenqu was implicated in Chenhao's affair and arrested at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chenqu was implicated in Chenhao's affair and imprisoned at Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 兄拱枘請以身代，拱榣佐之，卒得白。

translations.literal: His elder brother Gong Rui asked to take his place in punishment; Gong Rong assisted, and in the end innocence was established.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Gong Rui asked to suffer punishment in his stead; Gong Rong assisted, and in the end their innocence was established.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年上書請建宗學，令宗室設壇墠，行耕桑禮，謹祀典，加意恤刑，皆得旨俞允。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing he memorialized asking to establish a clan school, have the imperial clan set altars and perform farming and sericulture rites, observe sacrifices with care, and show special concern in criminal mercy—all were approved by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiajing he memorialized to establish a clan school, have the imperial clan set altars and perform farming and sericulture rites, observe sacrifices carefully, and temper punishments—all approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 捐田白鹿洞贍學者。

translations.literal: He donated fields at White Deer Grotto to support scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He donated fields at White Deer Grotto to support students.

sentences.zh: 其後以議禮稱旨，拱枘上大禮頌，並賜敕褒諭。

translations.literal: Later, because his views on the Rites Controversy pleased the throne, Gong Rui submitted Great Rites Eulogy and both received edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his views on the Rites Controversy pleased the throne, Gong Rui submitted Great Rites Eulogy and both received imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 諸子羣從多知名者。

translations.literal: Many sons and cousins became well known.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his sons and cousins became well known.

sentences.zh: 多熅、多燩以孝友著。

translations.literal: Duoyun and Duocan were noted for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Duoyun and Duocan were famed for filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 多煪、多𤆼以秉禮嚴重稱。

translations.literal: Duomei and Duoxuan were praised for holding to ritual with solemn dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Duomei and Duoxuan were praised for solemn adherence to ritual.

sentences.zh: 多𤏳、多煃、多炘以善詞賦名。

translations.literal: Duochong, Duokui, and Duoxin were famed for skill in poetry and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Duochong, Duokui, and Duoxin were famed for poetry and rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 而多熅與從兄多煡獨杜門却掃，多購異書，校讐以為樂。

translations.literal: Yet Duoyun and his elder cousin Duomei alone shut their doors and swept the path; they bought many rare books and took collating texts as their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Duoyun and his elder cousin Duomei alone shut their doors to the world, bought rare books, and found joy in collating texts.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，督撫薦理瑞昌王府事，謝不起。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign the governor and grand coordinator recommended him to administer Ruichang princely affairs, but he declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign the governor and grand coordinator recommended him to administer Ruichang princely affairs, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 多煪父拱樛以宸濠事被逮，多煪甫十餘齡，哭走軍門，乞以身代，王守仁見而異之。

translations.literal: Duomei's father Gong Jiao was arrested over the Chenhao affair when Duomei was barely ten; he wept and ran to the army gate begging to take his father's place, and Wang Shouren was struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: Duomei's father Gong Jiao was arrested in the Chenhao affair when Duomei was barely ten; he wept and ran to the army gate begging to suffer in his father's place, and Wang Shouren was moved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年疏訟父冤，得釋歸，復爵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he memorialized to plead his father's innocence; release was granted and his title restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing he memorialized pleading his father's innocence; his father was released and his title restored.

sentences.zh: 時諸郡王統於弋陽，而瑞昌始王不祀。

translations.literal: At the time commandery princes were all under Yiyang, yet Ruichang's founding prince was not enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: At the time commandery princes all fell under Yiyang, yet Ruichang's founding prince went without sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 多煪自謂小宗宜典宗祏，請於朝，特敕許焉。

translations.literal: Duomei held that as a lesser lineage he ought to maintain the ancestral shrine and petitioned the court; a special edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Duomei held that as a lesser lineage he should maintain the ancestral shrine and petitioned the court; a special edict approved.

sentences.zh: 乃益祭田，修飭家政，儼若朝典。

translations.literal: He then increased sacrificial fields, restored household discipline, and conducted affairs as solemnly as court ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He increased sacrificial fields, restored household discipline, and conducted affairs with the solemnity of court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 四子皆莊謹嗜學。

translations.literal: His four sons were all upright, careful, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: All four of his sons were upright, careful, and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 奉國將軍多煌，惠王第五子弋陽王奠壏五世孫也。

translations.literal: State Supporter General Duohuang was the fifth-generation descendant of Prince of Yiyang Dianjian, fifth son of Prince Hui.
translations.idiomatic: State Supporter General Duohuang was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince of Yiyang Dianjian, fifth son of Prince Hui.

sentences.zh: 孝友嗜學。

translations.literal: Filial, friendly, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial, affectionate, and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 弋陽五傳而絕，宗人舉多煌賢能，敕攝府事，瑞昌諸宗皆屬焉。

translations.literal: When the Yiyang line ended after five generations the clansmen nominated Duohuang for worth and ability; an edict ordered him to administer the princely household, and all the Ruichang clansmen were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yiyang line ended after five generations the clansmen nominated Duohuang as worthy and capable; an edict ordered him to administer the household, and all Ruichang clansmen were placed under him.

sentences.zh: 性廉靜寡欲，淑人熊氏早卒，不再娶，獨處齋閣者二十六年。

translations.literal: By nature he was incorrupt, quiet, and of few desires; the virtuous Lady Xiong died early and he never remarried, dwelling alone in his study for twenty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: Incorrupt, quiet, and of few desires, he never remarried after his virtuous wife Lady Xiong died young, and lived alone in his study for twenty-six years.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十一年，撫、按以行誼聞。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli the governor and censor reported his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Wanli the governor and censor reported his upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 詔褒之。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 會病卒，詔守臣加祭一壇。

translations.literal: When he fell ill and died an edict ordered the local officials to add one sacrificial altar.
translations.idiomatic: When he died of illness an edict ordered local officials to add one sacrificial altar.

sentences.zh: 又多炡者，亦奉國將軍，潁敏善詩歌，嘗變姓名出遊，蹤跡遍吳、楚。

translations.literal: There was also Duozheng, likewise a State Supporter General—clever and skilled in poetry and song; he once changed his name and traveled incognito, his tracks reaching all of Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Duozheng, a State Supporter General—clever and skilled in poetry; he once traveled incognito under another name, his tracks reaching all of Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 晚病羸，猶不廢吟誦。

translations.literal: In late life, though sick and weak, he still did not cease recitation.
translations.idiomatic: In late life, though frail with illness, he never ceased composing verse.

sentences.zh: 卒，門人私諡曰清敏先生。

translations.literal: When he died his disciples privately posthumously styled him Master Qingmin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his disciples privately gave him the posthumous style Master Qingmin.

sentences.zh: 子謀堚亦有父風。

translations.literal: His son Mou Jie also had his father's character.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mou Jie inherited his father's character.

sentences.zh: 時樂安輔國將軍多𤉰有詩癖，與謀堚等放志文酒，終其世。

translations.literal: At the time State Defender General Duohuan of Le'an had a passion for poetry and with Mou Jie and others gave themselves to literature and wine to the end of their days.
translations.idiomatic: At the time State Defender General Duohuan of Le'an was obsessed with poetry and with Mou Jie and others devoted themselves to literature and wine for the rest of their lives.
